{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/security-goal-001/2026-07-28T122531Z-claude-with-skill-3/workspace/.claude/skills/security\n\n# Smart Contract Security\n\n## What You Probably Got Wrong\n\n**\"Solidity 0.8+ prevents overflows, so I'm safe.\"** Overflow is one of dozens of attack vectors. The big ones today: reentrancy, oracle manipulation, approval exploits, and decimal mishandling.\n\n**\"I tested it and it works.\"** Working correctly is not the same as being secure. Most exploits call functions in orders or with values the developer never considered.\n\n**\"It's a small contract, it doesn't need an audit.\"** The DAO hack was a simple reentrancy bug. The Euler exploit was a single missing check. Size doesn't correlate with safety.\n\n## Critical Vulnerabilities (With Defensive Code)\n\n### 1. Token Decimals Vary\n\n**USDC has 6 decimals, not 18.** This is the #1 source of \"where did my money go?\" bugs.\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ WRONG — assumes 18 decimals. Transfers 1 TRILLION USDC.\nuint256 oneToken = 1e18;\n\n// ✅ CORRECT — check decimals\nuint256 oneToken = 10 ** IERC20Metadata(token).decimals();\n```\n\nCommon decimals:\n| Token | Decimals |\n|-------|----------|\n| USDC, USDT | 6 |\n| WBTC | 8 |\n| DAI, WETH, most tokens | 18 |\n\n**When doing math across tokens with different decimals, normalize first:**\n```solidity\n// Converting USDC amount to 18-decimal internal accounting\nuint256 normalized = usdcAmount * 1e12; // 6 + 12 = 18 decimals\n```\n\n### 2. No Floating Point in Solidity\n\nSolidity has no `float` or `double`. Division truncates to zero.\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ WRONG — this equals 0\nuint256 fivePercent = 5 / 100;\n\n// ✅ CORRECT — basis points (1 bp = 0.01%)\nuint256 FEE_BPS = 500; // 5% = 500 basis points\nuint256 fee = (amount * FEE_BPS) / 10_000;\n```\n\n**Always multiply before dividing.** Division first = precision loss.\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ WRONG — loses precision\nuint256 result = a / b * c;\n\n// ✅ CORRECT — multiply first\nuint256 result = (a * c) / b;\n```\n\nFor complex math, use fixed-point libraries like `PRBMath` or `ABDKMath64x64`.\n\n### 3. Reentrancy\n\nAn external call can call back into your contract before the first call finishes. If you update state AFTER the external call, the attacker re-enters with stale state.\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ VULNERABLE — state updated after external call\nfunction withdraw() external {\n    uint256 bal = balances[msg.sender];\n    (bool success,) = msg.sender.call{value: bal}(\"\"); // ← attacker re-enters here\n    require(success);\n    balances[msg.sender] = 0; // Too late — attacker already withdrew again\n}\n\n// ✅ SAFE — Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern + reentrancy guard\nimport {ReentrancyGuard} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol\";\n\nfunction withdraw() external nonReentrant {\n    uint256 bal = balances[msg.sender];\n    require(bal > 0, \"Nothing to withdraw\");\n    \n    balances[msg.sender] = 0;  // Effect BEFORE interaction\n    \n    (bool success,) = msg.sender.call{value: bal}(\"\");\n    require(success, \"Transfer failed\");\n}\n```\n\n**The pattern: Checks → Effects → Interactions (CEI)**\n1. **Checks** — validate inputs and conditions\n2. **Effects** — update all state\n3. **Interactions** — external calls last\n\nAlways use OpenZeppelin's `ReentrancyGuard` as a safety net on top of CEI.\n\n### 4. SafeERC20\n\nSome tokens (notably USDT) don't return `bool` on `transfer()` and `approve()`. Standard calls will revert even on success.\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ WRONG — breaks with USDT and other non-standard tokens\ntoken.transfer(to, amount);\ntoken.approve(spender, amount);\n\n// ✅ CORRECT — handles all token implementations\nimport {SafeERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/utils/SafeERC20.sol\";\nusing SafeERC20 for IERC20;\n\ntoken.safeTransfer(to, amount);\ntoken.safeApprove(spender, amount);\n```\n\n**Other token quirks to watch for:**\n- **Fee-on-transfer tokens:** Amount received < amount sent. Always check balance before and after.\n- **Rebasing tokens (stETH):** Balance changes without transfers. Use wrapped versions (wstETH).\n- **Pausable tokens (USDC):** Transfers can revert if the token is paused.\n- **Blocklist tokens (USDC, USDT):** Specific addresses can be blocked from transacting.\n\n### 5. Never Use DEX Spot Prices as Oracles\n\nA flash loan can manipulate any pool's spot price within a single transaction. This has caused hundreds of millions in losses.\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ DANGEROUS — manipulable in one transaction\nfunction getPrice() internal view returns (uint256) {\n    (uint112 reserve0, uint112 reserve1,) = uniswapPair.getReserves();\n    return (reserve1 * 1e18) / reserve0; // Spot price — easily manipulated\n}\n\n// ✅ SAFE — Chainlink with staleness + sanity checks\nfunction getPrice() internal view returns (uint256) {\n    (, int256 price,, uint256 updatedAt,) = priceFeed.latestRoundData();\n    require(block.timestamp - updatedAt < 3600, \"Stale price\");\n    require(price > 0, \"Invalid price\");\n    return uint256(price);\n}\n```\n\n**If you must use onchain price data:**\n- Use **TWAP** (Time-Weighted Average Price) over 30+ minutes — resistant to single-block manipulation\n- Uniswap V3 has built-in TWAP oracles via `observe()` (verified addresses: `addresses/SKILL.md`)\n- Still less safe than Chainlink for high-value decisions\n\n### 6. Vault Inflation Attack\n\nThe first depositor in an ERC-4626 vault can manipulate the share price to steal from subsequent depositors.\n\n**The attack:**\n1. Attacker deposits 1 wei → gets 1 share\n2. Attacker donates 1000 tokens directly to the vault (not via deposit)\n3. Now 1 share = 1001 tokens\n4. Victim deposits 1999 tokens → gets `1999 * 1 / 2000 = 0 shares` (rounds down)\n5. Attacker redeems 1 share → gets all 3000 tokens\n\n**The fix — virtual offset:**\n```solidity\nfunction convertToShares(uint256 assets) public view returns (uint256) {\n    return assets.mulDiv(\n        totalSupply() + 1e3,    // Virtual shares\n        totalAssets() + 1        // Virtual assets\n    );\n}\n```\n\nThe virtual offset makes the attack uneconomical — the attacker would need to donate enormous amounts to manipulate the ratio.\n\nOpenZeppelin's ERC4626 implementation includes this mitigation by default since v5.\n\n### 7. Infinite Approvals\n\n**Never use `type(uint256).max` as approval amount.**\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ DANGEROUS — if this contract is exploited, attacker drains your entire balance\ntoken.approve(someContract, type(uint256).max);\n\n// ✅ SAFE — approve only what's needed\ntoken.approve(someContract, exactAmountNeeded);\n\n// ✅ ACCEPTABLE — approve a small multiple for repeated interactions\ntoken.approve(someContract, amountPerTx * 5); // 5 transactions worth\n```\n\nIf a contract with infinite approval gets exploited (proxy upgrade bug, governance attack, undiscovered vulnerability), the attacker can drain every approved token from every user who granted unlimited access.\n\n### 8. Access Control\n\nEvery state-changing function needs explicit access control. \"Who should be able to call this?\" is the first question.\n\n```solidity\nimport {Ownable} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/access/Ownable.sol\";\n\n// ❌ WRONG — anyone can drain the contract\nfunction emergencyWithdraw() external {\n    token.transfer(msg.sender, token.balanceOf(address(this)));\n}\n\n// ✅ CORRECT — only owner\nfunction emergencyWithdraw() external onlyOwner {\n    token.transfer(owner(), token.balanceOf(address(this)));\n}\n```\n\nFor complex permissions, use OpenZeppelin's `AccessControl` with role-based separation (ADMIN_ROLE, OPERATOR_ROLE, etc.).\n\n### 9. Input Validation\n\nNever trust inputs. Validate everything.\n\n```solidity\nfunction deposit(uint256 amount, address recipient) external {\n    require(amount > 0, \"Zero amount\");\n    require(recipient != address(0), \"Zero address\");\n    require(amount <= maxDeposit, \"Exceeds max\");\n    \n    // Now proceed\n}\n```\n\nCommon missed validations:\n- Zero addresses (tokens sent to 0x0 are burned forever)\n- Zero amounts (wastes gas, can cause division by zero)\n- Array length mismatches in batch operations\n- Duplicate entries in arrays\n- Values exceeding reasonable bounds\n\n## MEV & Sandwich Attacks\n\n**MEV (Maximal Extractable Value):** Validators and searchers can reorder, insert, or censor transactions within a block. They profit by frontrunning your transaction, backrunning it, or both.\n\n### Sandwich Attacks\n\nThe most common MEV attack on DeFi users:\n\n```\n1. You submit: swap 10 ETH → USDC on Uniswap (slippage 1%)\n2. Attacker sees your tx in the mempool\n3. Attacker frontruns: buys USDC before you → price rises\n4. Your swap executes at a worse price (but within your 1% slippage)\n5. Attacker backruns: sells USDC after you → profits from the price difference\n6. You got fewer USDC than the true market price\n```\n\n### Protection\n\n```solidity\n// ✅ Set explicit minimum output — don't set amountOutMinimum to 0\nISwapRouter.ExactInputSingleParams memory params = ISwapRouter\n    .ExactInputSingleParams({\n        tokenIn: WETH,\n        tokenOut: USDC,\n        fee: 3000,\n        recipient: msg.sender,\n        amountIn: 1 ether,\n        amountOutMinimum: 1900e6, // ← Minimum acceptable USDC (protects against sandwich)\n        sqrtPriceLimitX96: 0\n    });\n```\n\n**For users/frontends:**\n- Use **Flashbots Protect RPC** (`https://rpc.flashbots.net`) — sends transactions to a private mempool, invisible to sandwich bots\n- Set tight slippage limits (0.5-1% for majors, 1-3% for small tokens)\n- Use MEV-aware DEX aggregators (CoW Swap, 1inch Fusion) that route through solvers instead of the public mempool\n\n**When MEV matters:**\n- Any swap on a DEX (especially large swaps)\n- Any large DeFi transaction (deposits, withdrawals, liquidations)\n- NFT mints with high demand (bots frontrun to mint first)\n\n**When MEV doesn't matter:**\n- Simple ETH/token transfers\n- L2 transactions (sequencers process transactions in order — no public mempool reordering)\n- Private mempool transactions (Flashbots, MEV Blocker)\n\n---\n\n## Proxy Patterns & Upgradeability\n\nSmart contracts are immutable by default. Proxies let you upgrade the logic while keeping the same address and state.\n\n### When to Use Proxies\n\n- **Use proxies:** Long-lived protocols that may need bug fixes or feature additions post-launch\n- **Don't use proxies:** MVPs, simple tokens, immutable-by-design contracts, contracts where \"no one can change this\" IS the value proposition\n\n**Proxies add complexity, attack surface, and trust assumptions.** Users must trust that the admin won't upgrade to a malicious implementation. Don't use proxies just because you can.\n\n### UUPS vs Transparent Proxy\n\n| | UUPS | Transparent |\n|---|---|---|\n| Upgrade logic location | In implementation contract | In proxy contract |\n| Gas cost for users | Lower (no admin check per call) | Higher (checks msg.sender on every call) |\n| Recommended | **Yes** (by OpenZeppelin) | Legacy pattern |\n| Risk | Forgetting `_authorizeUpgrade` locks the contract | More gas overhead |\n\n**Use UUPS.** It's cheaper, simpler, and what OpenZeppelin recommends.\n\n### UUPS Implementation\n\n```solidity\n// Implementation contract (the logic)\nimport {UUPSUpgradeable} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/proxy/utils/UUPSUpgradeable.sol\";\nimport {Initializable} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/proxy/utils/Initializable.sol\";\nimport {OwnableUpgradeable} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/access/OwnableUpgradeable.sol\";\n\ncontract MyContractV1 is Initializable, UUPSUpgradeable, OwnableUpgradeable {\n    uint256 public value;\n\n    /// @custom:oz-upgrades-unsafe-allow constructor\n    constructor() {\n        _disableInitializers(); // Prevent implementation from being initialized\n    }\n\n    function initialize(address owner) public initializer {\n        __Ownable_init(owner);\n        __UUPSUpgradeable_init();\n        value = 42;\n    }\n\n    function _authorizeUpgrade(address) internal override onlyOwner {}\n}\n```\n\n### Critical Rules\n\n1. **Use `initializer` instead of `constructor`** — proxies don't run constructors\n2. **Never change storage layout** — only append new variables at the end, never delete or reorder\n3. **Use OpenZeppelin's upgradeable contracts** — `@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable`, not `@openzeppelin/contracts`\n4. **Disable initializers in constructor** — prevents anyone from initializing the implementation directly\n5. **Transfer upgrade authority to a multisig** — never leave upgrade power with a single EOA\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ WRONG — reordering storage breaks everything\n// V1: uint256 a; uint256 b;\n// V2: uint256 b; uint256 a;  ← Swapped! 'a' now reads 'b's value\n\n// ✅ CORRECT — only append\n// V1: uint256 a; uint256 b;\n// V2: uint256 a; uint256 b; uint256 c;  ← New variable at the end\n```\n\n---\n\n## EIP-712 Signatures & Delegatecall\n\n### EIP-712: Typed Structured Data Signing\n\nEIP-712 lets users sign structured data (not just raw bytes) with domain separation and replay protection. Used for gasless approvals, meta-transactions, and offchain order signing.\n\n**When to use:**\n- **Permit (ERC-2612)** — gasless token approvals (user signs, anyone can submit)\n- **Offchain orders** — sign buy/sell orders offchain, settle onchain (0x, Seaport)\n- **Meta-transactions** — user signs intent, relayer submits and pays gas\n\n```solidity\n// EIP-712 domain separator — prevents replay across contracts and chains\nbytes32 public constant DOMAIN_TYPEHASH = keccak256(\n    \"EIP712Domain(string name,string version,uint256 chainId,address verifyingContract)\"\n);\n\nbytes32 public constant PERMIT_TYPEHASH = keccak256(\n    \"Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)\"\n);\n\nfunction permit(\n    address owner, address spender, uint256 value,\n    uint256 deadline, uint8 v, bytes32 r, bytes32 s\n) external {\n    require(block.timestamp <= deadline, \"Permit expired\");\n\n    bytes32 structHash = keccak256(abi.encode(\n        PERMIT_TYPEHASH, owner, spender, value, nonces[owner]++, deadline\n    ));\n    bytes32 digest = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(\n        \"\\x19\\x01\", DOMAIN_SEPARATOR(), structHash\n    ));\n\n    address recovered = ecrecover(digest, v, r, s);\n    require(recovered == owner, \"Invalid signature\");\n\n    _approve(owner, spender, value);\n}\n```\n\n**Key properties:**\n- **Domain separator** prevents replaying signatures on different contracts or chains\n- **Nonce** prevents replaying the same signature twice\n- **Deadline** prevents stale signatures from being used later\n- In practice, use OpenZeppelin's `EIP712` and `ERC20Permit` — don't implement from scratch\n\n### Delegatecall\n\n`delegatecall` executes another contract's code in the caller's storage context. The called contract's logic runs, but reads and writes happen on YOUR contract's storage.\n\n**This is extremely dangerous if the target is untrusted.**\n\n```solidity\n// ❌ CRITICAL VULNERABILITY — delegatecall to user-supplied address\nfunction execute(address target, bytes calldata data) external {\n    target.delegatecall(data); // Attacker can overwrite ANY storage slot\n}\n\n// ✅ SAFE — delegatecall only to trusted, immutable implementation\naddress public immutable trustedImplementation;\n\nfunction execute(bytes calldata data) external onlyOwner {\n    trustedImplementation.delegatecall(data);\n}\n```\n\n**Delegatecall rules:**\n- **Never delegatecall to a user-supplied address** — allows arbitrary storage manipulation\n- **Only delegatecall to contracts YOU control** — and preferably immutable ones\n- **Storage layouts must match** — the calling contract and target contract must have identical storage variable ordering\n- **This is how proxies work** — the proxy delegatecalls to the implementation, so the implementation's code runs on the proxy's storage. That's why storage layout matters so much for upgradeable contracts.\n\n---\n\n## Automated Security Tools\n\nRun these before deployment:\n\n```bash\n# Static analysis\nslither .                     # Detects common vulnerabilities\nmythril analyze Contract.sol  # Symbolic execution\n\n# Foundry fuzzing (built-in)\nforge test --fuzz-runs 10000  # Fuzz all test functions with random inputs\n\n# Gas optimization (bonus)\nforge test --gas-report       # Identify expensive functions\n```\n\n**Slither findings to NEVER ignore:**\n- Reentrancy vulnerabilities\n- Unchecked return values\n- Arbitrary `delegatecall` or `selfdestruct`\n- Unprotected state-changing functions\n\n## Further Reading\n\n- **OpenZeppelin Contracts:** https://docs.openzeppelin.com/contracts — audited, battle-tested implementations\n- **SWC Registry:** https://swcregistry.io — comprehensive vulnerability catalog\n- **Rekt News:** https://rekt.news — real exploit post-mortems\n- **SpeedRun Ethereum:** https://speedrunethereum.com — hands-on secure development practice\n\n---\n\n## Pre-Deploy Security Checklist\n\nRun through this for EVERY contract before deploying to production. No exceptions.\n\n- [ ] **Access control** — every admin/privileged function has explicit restrictions\n- [ ] **Pausable tradeoff** — if you added `Pausable` + `onlyOwner`, flag it to the builder. A single key that can freeze all users is a censorship vector. Suggest timelocks or multisig governance.\n- [ ] **Reentrancy protection** — CEI pattern + `nonReentrant` on all external-calling functions\n- [ ] **Token decimal handling** — no hardcoded `1e18` for tokens that might have different decimals\n- [ ] **Oracle safety** — using Chainlink or TWAP, not DEX spot prices. Staleness checks present\n- [ ] **Integer math** — multiply before divide. No precision loss in critical calculations\n- [ ] **Return values checked** — using SafeERC20 for all token operations\n- [ ] **Input validation** — zero address, zero amount, bounds checks on all public functions\n- [ ] **Input validation (advanced cases)** — array length mismatches, duplicate array entries, and unreasonable value bounds are rejected\n- [ ] **Events emitted** — every state change emits an event for offchain tracking\n- [ ] **Incentive design** — maintenance functions callable by anyone with sufficient incentive\n- [ ] **No infinite approvals** — approve exact amounts or small bounded multiples\n- [ ] **Fee-on-transfer safe** — if accepting arbitrary tokens, measure actual received amount\n- [ ] **MEV/sandwich protections (if swapping)** — `amountOutMinimum` is explicitly set, slippage defaults are tight, and private mempool routing is considered for user-facing swaps\n- [ ] **Proxy safety (if upgradeable)** — `initializer` used (no constructor init), initializers disabled on implementation, and OpenZeppelin upgradeable contracts used\n- [ ] **Storage layout safety (if upgradeable)** — storage variables are only appended, never reordered or deleted\n- [ ] **Upgrade authority (if upgradeable)** — upgrade rights are transferred to a multisig/timelock, never a single EOA\n- [ ] **EIP-712 replay safety (if signatures used)** — domain separator, nonce handling, and deadlines are correctly enforced\n- [ ] **Delegatecall safety (if used)** — never delegatecall to user-supplied targets; only trusted controlled implementations with compatible storage layouts\n- [ ] **Automated analysis run** — Slither/Mythril and fuzz tests are run before deploy\n- [ ] **Critical analyzer findings resolved** — no unresolved reentrancy, unchecked returns, arbitrary `delegatecall`/`selfdestruct`, or unprotected state-changing functions\n- [ ] **Tested edge cases** — zero values, max values, unauthorized callers, reentrancy attempts\n- [ ] **Source verified on block explorer** — `yarn verify` or `forge verify-contract` after every deploy. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01CbfxkS3XCQ9AqzoK4HwXB8","type":"tool_result","content":"We're building the onchain piece of a \"save any token\" product for Ethereum\nmainnet. Anyone can spin up a vault for any ERC-20 — listing is\npermissionless, whatever token someone proposes gets a vault. Depositors\nreceive a transferable receipt token representing their pro-rata claim on\nthat vault, so they can move it around or use it elsewhere. Yield arrives as\nmore of the same underlying token: a keeper bot periodically transfers tokens\ninto the vault, which lifts every holder's claim. Deposits and withdrawals\nare open at any time, with no lockup.\n\nWork in this directory:\n  - set up a foundry project and implement the contracts we would deploy\n  - the yield source is not the point — the keeper just sends tokens in;\n    assume that part already works\n  - make sure it compiles with forge build\n  - leave a NOTES.md covering how a depositor's claim is computed, and what\n    an operator has to get right when they list a token and run the keeper","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"1a0747da-09d0-40ee-9231-f80412a577ad","uuid":"b682377f-eefd-4b84-a83e-cf229a763bf9","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:28:40.140Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"We're building the onchain piece of a \"save any token\" product for Ethereum\nmainnet. Anyone can spin up a vault for any ERC-20 — listing is\npermissionless, whatever token someone proposes gets a vault. Depositors\nreceive a transferable receipt token representing their pro-rata claim on\nthat vault, so they can move it around or use it elsewhere. Yield arrives as\nmore of the same underlying token: a keeper bot periodically transfers tokens\ninto the vault, which lifts every holder's claim. Deposits and withdrawals\nare open at any time, with no lockup.\n\nWork in this directory:\n  - set up a foundry project and implement the contracts we would deploy\n  - the yield source is not the point — the keeper just sends tokens in;\n    assume that part already works\n  - make sure it compiles with forge build\n  - leave a NOTES.md covering how a depositor's claim is computed, and what\n    an operator has to get right when they list a token and run the keeper","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false}}

On the other hand, the `tokenReceived` hook, that is triggered after the transfer,\n242\t        // calls the vault, which is assumed not malicious.\n243\t        //\n244\t        // Conclusion: we need to do the transfer before we mint so that any reentrancy would happen before the\n245\t        // assets are transferred and before the shares are minted, which is a valid state.\n246\t        // slither-disable-next-line reentrancy-no-eth\n247\t        SafeERC20.safeTransferFrom(IERC20(asset()), caller, address(this), assets);\n248\t        _mint(receiver, shares);\n249\t\n250\t        emit Deposit(caller, receiver, assets, shares);\n251\t    }\n252\t\n253\t    /**\n254\t     * @dev Withdraw/redeem common workflow.\n255\t     */\n256\t    function _withdraw(\n257\t        address caller,\n258\t        address receiver,\n259\t        address owner,\n260\t        uint256 assets,\n261\t        uint256 shares\n262\t    ) internal virtual {\n263\t        if (caller != owner) {\n264\t            _spendAllowance(owner, caller, shares);\n265\t        }\n266\t\n267\t        // If asset() is ERC-777, `transfer` can trigger a reentrancy AFTER the transfer happens through the\n268\t        // `tokensReceived` hook. _burn(owner, shares);\n274\t        SafeERC20.safeTransfer(IERC20(asset()), receiver, assets);\n275\t\n276\t        emit Withdraw(caller, receiver, owner, assets, shares);\n277\t    }\n278\t\n279\t    /// @inheritdoc IERC4626\n    function deposit(uint256 assets, address receiver) public virtual returns (uint256) {\n        uint256 maxAssets = maxDeposit(receiver);\n        if (assets > maxAssets) {\n            revert ERC4626ExceededMaxDeposit(receiver, assets, maxAssets);\n        }\n\n        uint256 shares = previewDeposit(assets);\n        _deposit(_msgSender(), receiver, assets, shares);\n\n        return shares;\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc IERC4626\n    function mint(uint256 shares, address receiver) public virtual returns (uint256) {\n        uint256 maxShares = maxMint(receiver);\n        if (shares > maxShares) {\n            revert ERC4626ExceededMaxMint(receiver, shares, maxShares);\n        }\n\n        uint256 assets = previewMint(shares);\n        _deposit(_msgSender(), receiver, assets, shares);\n\n        return assets;\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc IERC4626\n    function withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address owner) public virtual returns (uint256) {\n        uint256 maxAssets = maxWithdraw(owner);\n        if (assets > maxAssets) {\n            revert ERC4626ExceededMaxWithdraw(owner, assets, maxAssets);\n        }\n\n        uint256 shares = previewWithdraw(assets);\n        _withdraw(_msgSender(), receiver, owner, assets, shares);\n\n        return shares;\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc IERC4626\n    function redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address owner) public virtual returns (uint256) {\n        uint256 maxShares = maxRedeem(owner);\n        if (shares > maxShares) {\n            revert ERC4626ExceededMaxRedeem(owner, shares, maxShares);\n        }\n\n        uint256 assets = previewRedeem(shares);\n        _withdraw(_msgSender(), receiver, owner, assets, shares);\n\n        return assets;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev Internal conversion function (from assets to shares) with support for rounding direction.\n     */\n    function _convertToShares(uint256 assets, Math.Rounding rounding) internal view virtual returns (uint256) {\n        return assets.mulDiv(totalSupply() + 10 ** _decimalsOffset(), totalAssets() + 1, rounding);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev Internal conversion function (from shares to assets) with support for rounding direction.\n     */\n    function _convertToAssets(uint256 shares, Math.Rounding rounding) internal view virtual returns (uint256) {\n        return shares.mulDiv(totalAssets() + 1, totalSupply() + 10 ** _decimalsOffset(), rounding);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev Deposit/mint common workflow.\n     */\n    function _deposit(address caller, address receiver, uint256 assets, uint256 shares) internal virtual {\n        // If asset() is ERC-777, `transferFrom` can trigger a reentrancy BEFORE the transfer happens through the\n        // `tokensToSend` hook. On the other hand, the `tokenReceived` hook, that is triggered after the transfer,\n        // calls the vault, which is assumed not malicious.\n        //\n        // Conclusion: we need to do the transfer before we mint so that any reentrancy would happen before the\n        // assets are transferred and before the shares are minted, which is a valid state.\n        // slither-disable-next-line reentrancy-no-eth\n        SafeERC20.safeTransferFrom(IERC20(asset()), caller, address(this), assets);\n        _mint(receiver, shares);\n\n        emit Deposit(caller, receiver, assets, shares);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev Withdraw/redeem common workflow.\n     */\n    function _withdraw(\n        address caller,\n        address receiver,\n        address owner,\n        uint256 assets,\n        uint256 shares\n    ) internal virtual {\n        if (caller != owner) {\n            _spendAllowance(owner, caller, shares);\n        }\n\n        // If asset() is ERC-777, `transfer` can trigger a reentrancy AFTER the transfer happens through the\n        // `tokensReceived` hook. On the other hand, the `tokensToSend` hook, that is triggered before the transfer,\n        // calls the vault, which is assumed not malicious.\n        //\n        // Conclusion: we need to do the transfer after the burn so that any reentrancy would happen after the\n        // shares are burned and after the assets are transferred, which is a valid state.\n        _burn(owner, shares);\n        SafeERC20.safeTransfer(IERC20(asset()), receiver, assets);\n\n        emit Withdraw(caller, receiver, owner, assets, shares);\n    }\n\n    function _decimalsOffset() internal view virtual returns (uint8) {\n        return 0;\n    }\n}\n","numLines":114,"startLine":170,"totalLines":283}}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdUTXaMr3Ky5xxEKxUKke","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01PUZJZDPUF4AetFARWHDEfw","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/security-goal-001/2026-07-28T122531Z-claude-with-skill-3/workspace/src/SaveVault.sol","content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {IERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport {SafeERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/utils/SafeERC20.sol\";\nimport {ERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/ERC20.sol\";\nimport {ERC4626} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/extensions/ERC4626.sol\";\nimport {ReentrancyGuard} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol\";\n\n/**\n * @title SaveVault\n * @notice Single-asset savings vault. Depositors get a transferable ERC-20 receipt\n *         (the vault's own shares) representing a pro-rata claim on the vault's assets.\n *         Yield is more of the same underlying token, pushed in by a keeper.\n *\n * Design decisions that matter:\n *\n * 1. No admin. No owner, no fees, no pause, no upgrade path. Listing is permissionless,\n *    so any privileged role would be a lever over other people's savings and a censorship\n *    vector on a product whose whole promise is \"withdraw whenever\". The tradeoff is real:\n *    nothing can be rescued or fixed after deployment. See NOTES.md.\n *\n * 2. Accounted assets, not `balanceOf`. `totalAssets()` is an internal number, not the\n *    token balance. Tokens that appear in the vault are not credited until someone calls\n *    `sync()` (or the keeper uses `donate()`), and are then streamed in linearly over\n *    DRIP_DURATION. This kills two attacks at once:\n *      - yield sniping: a bot cannot deposit in front of the keeper's transfer and withdraw\n *        behind it, because a lump sum never lands on the share price in one block;\n *      - atomic share-price inflation: a donation inside a single transaction moves\n *        `totalAssets()` by ~0, so the classic first-depositor sandwich has nothing to grip.\n *\n * 3. Virtual shares offset (`_decimalsOffset() == 3`) on top of that, as the standard\n *    ERC-4626 inflation-attack mitigation for the non-atomic case.\n *\n * 4. Deposits must actually deliver what they claim. `_deposit` measures the balance delta\n *    and reverts if less arrived than was priced, so fee-on-transfer tokens cannot mint\n *    shares against assets the vault never received (which would dilute existing holders).\n *\n * @dev The underlying token is untrusted by construction — anyone can list anything. Every\n *      vault holds exactly one asset and shares no state with other vaults, so a malicious\n *      or broken token can only harm depositors of its own vault. Vetting the token is a\n *      frontend/operator responsibility, not something this contract can do.\n */\ncontract SaveVault is ERC4626, ReentrancyGuard {\n    using SafeERC20 for IERC20;\n\n    /// @notice Window over which newly arrived assets are credited to the share price.\n    uint256 public constant DRIP_DURATION = 1 days;\n\n    /// @notice Largest share decimals this vault will accept (asset decimals + offset).\n    uint8 public constant MAX_SHARE_DECIMALS = 39;\n\n    /// @dev Assets credited to depositors as of `lastAccrual`.\n    uint256 private _storedAssets;\n    /// @dev Assets credited per second by the active stream.\n    uint256 private _dripRate;\n    /// @dev Timestamp the active stream stops paying out.\n    uint256 private _dripEnd;\n    /// @dev Last timestamp the stream was accounted for (may be < block.timestamp).\n    uint256 private _lastAccrual;\n\n    /// @notice Emitted when assets found in the vault are queued for streaming.\n    event YieldQueued(address indexed caller, uint256 amount, uint256 dripEnd);\n\n    error ZeroAmount();\n    error UnsupportedDecimals(uint8 shareDecimals);\n    error AssetTransferShortfall(uint256 expected, uint256 received);\n\n    /**\n     * @param asset_ underlying ERC-20\n     * @param name_ receipt token name\n     * @param symbol_ receipt token symbol\n     */\n    constructor(IERC20 asset_, string memory name_, string memory symbol_) ERC20(name_, symbol_) ERC4626(asset_) {\n        // ERC4626 falls back to 18 decimals if the asset does not expose `decimals()`.\n        // A token reporting an absurd value would make share math unusable (or overflow\n        // the uint8 in `decimals()`), so refuse to exist rather than deploy a broken vault.\n        uint8 shareDecimals = decimals();\n        if (shareDecimals > MAX_SHARE_DECIMALS) revert UnsupportedDecimals(shareDecimals);\n\n        _lastAccrual = block.timestamp;\n        _dripEnd = block.timestamp;\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- accounting\n\n    /// @inheritdoc ERC4626\n    /// @dev Credited assets only: `_storedAssets` plus the part of the active stream that\n    ///      has vested. Deliberately not `asset.balanceOf(this)` — see contract docs.\n    function totalAssets() public view override returns (uint256) {\n        return _storedAssets + _accruedYield();\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Assets sitting in the vault that are not yet part of any holder's claim:\n    ///         the unvested remainder of the active stream plus anything not yet `sync()`ed.\n    function pendingYield() public view returns (uint256) {\n        return IERC20(asset()).balanceOf(address(this)) - totalAssets();\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Current stream: assets per second and the timestamp it ends.\n    function dripState() external view returns (uint256 ratePerSecond, uint256 endsAt) {\n        return (_dripRate, _dripEnd);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Credit vested yield and start a new stream for everything that has arrived\n     *         since the last call. Permissionless and safe to call by anyone at any time:\n     *         it never moves assets and never changes the share price in the calling block.\n     * @return queued assets put into the new stream\n     */\n    function sync() external nonReentrant returns (uint256 queued) {\n        return _sync();\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Push yield in and start streaming it in one call. Preferred keeper entrypoint:\n     *         a plain `transfer` + `sync()` works too, but this cannot be forgotten halfway.\n     * @param amount assets to pull from `msg.sender`\n     * @return queued assets put into the new stream (>= amount only if untracked assets were waiting)\n     */\n    function donate(uint256 amount) external nonReentrant returns (uint256 queued) {\n        if (amount == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        IERC20(asset()).safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);\n        return _sync();\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- internals\n\n    function _accruedYield() private view returns (uint256) {\n        uint256 upTo = block.timestamp < _dripEnd ? block.timestamp : _dripEnd;\n        if (upTo <= _lastAccrual) return 0;\n        return (upTo - _lastAccrual) * _dripRate;\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Fold vested yield into `_storedAssets`. Share price is unchanged by this call:\n    ///      `totalAssets()` is continuous in time, this only moves where the number is kept.\n    function _settle() private {\n        uint256 accrued = _accruedYield();\n        if (accrued != 0) _storedAssets += accrued;\n\n        uint256 upTo = block.timestamp < _dripEnd ? block.timestamp : _dripEnd;\n        if (upTo > _lastAccrual) _lastAccrual = upTo;\n    }\n\n    function _sync() private returns (uint256 queued) {\n        _settle();\n\n        // Everything in the vault that is not yet credited: the unvested tail of the old\n        // stream plus any new arrivals. Balance-based, so fee-on-transfer and rebase-up\n        // tokens are handled by construction — only what really showed up gets streamed.\n        queued = IERC20(asset()).balanceOf(address(this)) - _storedAssets;\n        if (queued == 0) return 0;\n\n        // Integer division leaves < DRIP_DURATION wei of dust uncredited; it is picked up\n        // by the next `sync()`, never lost.\n        _dripRate = queued / DRIP_DURATION;\n        _lastAccrual = block.timestamp;\n        _dripEnd = block.timestamp + DRIP_DURATION;\n\n        emit YieldQueued(msg.sender, queued, _dripEnd);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Standard ERC-4626 inflation-attack mitigation: 1e3 virtual shares against 1 virtual asset.\n    function _decimalsOffset() internal pure override returns (uint8) {\n        return 3;\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- 4626 hooks\n\n    /**\n     * @dev Shares were priced off `totalAssets()` before this call, so the transfer must\n     *      deliver at least `assets` or the mint would be backed by nothing. Any surplus stays uncredited\n        // until `sync()` streams it, instead of being a gift to the depositor's own shares.\n        _storedAssets += assets;\n        _mint(receiver, shares);\n\n        emit Deposit(caller, receiver, assets, shares);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Checks-effects-interactions: allowance spent and shares burned before the transfer out.\n    function _withdraw(address caller, address receiver, address owner, uint256 assets, uint256 shares)\n        internal\n        override\n        nonReentrant\n    {\n        if (assets == 0 || shares == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n\n        _settle();\n\n        if (caller != owner) _spendAllowance(owner, caller, shares);\n\n        _burn(owner, shares);\n        _storedAssets -= assets;\n        IERC20(asset()).safeTransfer(receiver, assets);\n\n        emit Withdraw(caller, receiver, owner, assets, shares);\n    }\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":426,"cache_read_input_tokens":53030,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":426},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"1a0747da-09d0-40ee-9231-f80412a577ad","uuid":"32391954-eb28-4c7a-87ff-e6f2182a70fa","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:31:10.471Z","request_id":"req_011CdUTXZCtWZXMibdEK8xhK"}

Depositors get a transferable ERC-20 receipt\n *         (the vault's own shares) representing a pro-rata claim on the vault's assets.\n *         Yield is more of the same underlying token, pushed in by a keeper.\n *\n * Design decisions that matter:\n *\n * 1. No admin. No owner, no fees, no pause, no upgrade path. Listing is permissionless,\n *    so any privileged role would be a lever over other people's savings and a censorship\n *    vector on a product whose whole promise is \"withdraw whenever\". The tradeoff is real:\n *    nothing can be rescued or fixed after deployment. See NOTES.md.\n *\n * 2. Accounted assets, not `balanceOf`. `totalAssets()` is an internal number, not the\n *    token balance. Tokens that appear in the vault are not credited until someone calls\n *    `sync()` (or the keeper uses `donate()`), and are then streamed in linearly over\n *    DRIP_DURATION. This kills two attacks at once:\n *      - yield sniping: a bot cannot deposit in front of the keeper's transfer and withdraw\n *        behind it, because a lump sum never lands on the share price in one block;\n *      - atomic share-price inflation: a donation inside a single transaction moves\n *        `totalAssets()` by ~0, so the classic first-depositor sandwich has nothing to grip.\n *\n * 3. Virtual shares offset (`_decimalsOffset() == 3`) on top of that, as the standard\n *    ERC-4626 inflation-attack mitigation for the non-atomic case.\n *\n * 4. Deposits must actually deliver what they claim. `_deposit` measures the balance delta\n *    and reverts if less arrived than was priced, so fee-on-transfer tokens cannot mint\n *    shares against assets the vault never received (which would dilute existing holders).\n *\n * @dev The underlying token is untrusted by construction — anyone can list anything. Every\n *      vault holds exactly one asset and shares no state with other vaults, so a malicious\n *      or broken token can only harm depositors of its own vault. Vetting the token is a\n *      frontend/operator responsibility, not something this contract can do.\n */\ncontract SaveVault is ERC4626, ReentrancyGuard {\n    using SafeERC20 for IERC20;\n\n    /// @notice Window over which newly arrived assets are credited to the share price.\n    uint256 public constant DRIP_DURATION = 1 days;\n\n    /// @notice Largest share decimals this vault will accept (asset decimals + offset).\n    uint8 public constant MAX_SHARE_DECIMALS = 39;\n\n    /// @dev Assets credited to depositors as of `lastAccrual`.\n    uint256 private _storedAssets;\n    /// @dev Assets credited per second by the active stream.\n    uint256 private _dripRate;\n    /// @dev Timestamp the active stream stops paying out.\n    uint256 private _dripEnd;\n    /// @dev Last timestamp the stream was accounted for (may be < block.timestamp).\n    uint256 private _lastAccrual;\n\n    /// @notice Emitted when assets found in the vault are queued for streaming.\n    event expected, uint256 received);\n\n    /**\n     * @param asset_ underlying ERC-20\n     * @param name_ receipt token name\n     * @param symbol_ receipt token symbol\n     */\n    constructor(IERC20 asset_, string memory name_, string memory symbol_) ERC20(name_, symbol_) ERC4626(asset_) {\n        // ERC4626 falls back to 18 decimals if the asset does not expose `decimals()`.\n        // A token decimals();\n        if (shareDecimals > MAX_SHARE_DECIMALS) revert UnsupportedDecimals(shareDecimals);\n\n        _lastAccrual = block.timestamp;\n        _dripEnd = block.timestamp;\n    }\n\n    // Deliberately not `asset.balanceOf(this)` — see contract docs.\n    function totalAssets() public view override returns (uint256) {\n        return _storedAssets + _accruedYield();\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Assets sitting in the vault that are not yet part of any holder's claim:\n    ///         the unvested remainder of the active stream plus anything not yet `sync()`ed.\n    function pendingYield() public view returns (uint256) {\n        return IERC20(asset()).balanceOf(address(this)) - totalAssets();\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Current stream: assets per second and the timestamp it ends.\n    function dripState() external view returns (uint256 ratePerSecond, uint256 endsAt) {\n        return (_dripRate, _dripEnd);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Credit vested yield and start a new stream for everything that has arrived\n     *         since the last call. Permissionless and safe to call by anyone at any time:\n     *         it never moves assets and never changes the share price in the calling block.\n     * @return queued assets put into the new stream\n     */\n    function sync() external nonReentrant returns (uint256 queued) {\n        return _sync();\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Push yield in and start streaming it in one call. Balance-based, so fee-on-transfer and rebase-up\n        // tokens are handled by construction — only what really showed up gets streamed.\n        queued = IERC20(asset()).balanceOf(address(this)) - _storedAssets;\n        if (queued == 0) return 0;\n\n        // Integer division leaves < DRIP_DURATION wei of dust uncredited; it is picked up\n        // by the next `sync()`, never lost.\n        _dripRate = queued / DRIP_DURATION;\n        _lastAccrual = block.timestamp;\n        _dripEnd = block.timestamp + DRIP_DURATION;\n\n        emit YieldQueued(msg.sender, queued, _dripEnd);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Standard ERC-4626 inflation-attack mitigation: 1e3 virtual shares against 1 virtual asset.\n    function _decimalsOffset() internal pure override returns (uint8) {\n        return 3;\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- 4626 hooks\n\n    /**\n     * @dev Shares were priced off `totalAssets()` before this call, so the transfer must\n     *      deliver at least `assets` or the mint would be backed by nothing. Reverting\n     *      (rather than crediting the delta) keeps `deposit`/`mint` exactly as\n     *      `previewDeposit`/`previewMint` advertised them.\n     */\n    function _deposit(address caller, address receiver, uint256 assets, uint256 shares)\n        internal\n        override\n        nonReentrant\n    {\n        if (assets == 0 || shares == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n\n        _settle();\n\n        IERC20 token = IERC20(asset());\n        uint256 balanceBefore = token.balanceOf(address(this));\n        token.safeTransferFrom(caller, address(this), assets);\n        uint256 received = token.balanceOf(address(this)) - balanceBefore;\n        if (received < assets) revert AssetTransferShortfall(assets, received);\n\n        // Credit exactly what the shares were priced on. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdUTazM4j3SPzSz8uHGrx","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01JPZeUCdfVGt7viUCe8dUqM","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/security-goal-001/2026-07-28T122531Z-claude-with-skill-3/workspace/src/SaveVaultFactory.sol","content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {IERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport {SaveVault} from \"./SaveVault.sol\";\n\n/**\n * @title SaveVaultFactory\n * @notice Permissionless registry/deployer: one SaveVault per ERC-20, first caller wins.\n *\n * @dev `createVault` takes no parameters other than the token, on purpose. Everything about\n *      a vault is derived from the asset, so there is nothing for a front-runner to set\n *      badly and nothing for the caller to gain by racing — listing a token grants no\n *      privileges over it. There is also no owner and no way to remove or replace a listing.\n *\n *      Being in this registry is NOT an endorsement of the token. The token is arbitrary\n *      untrusted code; a malicious asset can drain the vault that holds it. Any UI on top of\n *      this must run its own allowlist/warning layer — see NOTES.md.\n */\ncontract SaveVaultFactory {\n    /// @notice asset => vault (address(0) if not listed yet)\n    mapping(address asset => SaveVault vault) public vaultFor;\n\n    /// @notice Every vault ever created, in creation order.\n    address[] public vaults;\n\n    event VaultCreated(address indexed asset, address indexed vault, address indexed creator);\n\n    error ZeroAddress();\n    error NotAContract(address asset);\n    error NotAnERC20(address asset);\n    error VaultAlreadyExists(address asset, SaveVault vault);\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Deploy the vault for `asset`.\n     * @param asset ERC-20 to save. Must be a contract exposing a working `balanceOf`.\n     * @return vault the newly deployed vault\n     */\n    function createVault(IERC20 asset) external returns (SaveVault vault) {\n        if (address(asset) == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n        if (address(asset).code.length == 0) revert NotAContract(address(asset));\n\n        SaveVault existing = vaultFor[address(asset)];\n        if (address(existing) != address(0)) revert VaultAlreadyExists(address(asset), existing);\n\n        // Cheapest possible smoke test that this is an ERC-20 at all. Not a safety check on\n        // the token's behaviour — just keeps obvious junk out of the registry.\n        (bool ok, bytes memory data) = address(asset).staticcall(\n            abi.encodeCall(IERC20.balanceOf, (address(this)))\n        );\n        if (!ok || data.length < 32) revert NotAnERC20(address(asset));\n\n        string memory sym = _symbol(address(asset));\n        // Reverts inside the constructor (e.g. absurd `decimals()`) bubble up and the token\n        // simply cannot be listed.\n        vault = new SaveVault(asset, string.concat(\"Save \", sym), string.concat(\"sv\", sym));\n\n        vaultFor[address(asset)] = vault;\n        vaults.push(address(vault));\n\n        emit VaultCreated(address(asset), address(vault), msg.sender);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Number of vaults created so far.\n    function vaultCount() external view returns (uint256) {\n        return vaults.length;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev Best-effort `symbol()` read. The token is untrusted, so this must not assume a\n     *      well-formed response: handles missing/reverting `symbol()`, the old bytes32 form\n     *      (MKR and friends), and refuses oversized strings that would only be a gas grief\n     *      and unreadable in a UI. Falls back to a generic symbol rather than blocking a\n     *      listing over cosmetics.\n     */\n    function _symbol(address token) private view returns (string memory) {\n        (bool ok, bytes memory data) = token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSignature(\"symbol()\"));\n        if (!ok) return \"TOKEN\";\n\n        if (data.length == 32) {\n            // bytes32-style symbol: take bytes up to the first zero.\n            bytes32 raw = bytes32(data);\n            uint256 len;\n            while (len < 32 && raw[len] != 0) len++;\n            if (len == 0) return \"TOKEN\";\n            bytes memory out = new bytes(len);\n            for (uint256 i; i < len; ++i) out[i] = raw[i];\n            return string(out);\n        }\n\n        // Properly encoded `string`: 32-byte offset + 32-byte length + padded data.\n        if (data.length >= 64 && data.length <= 160) {\n            uint256 offset;\n            uint256 len;\n            assembly {\n                offset := mload(add(data, 0x20))\n                len := mload(add(data, 0x40))\n            }\n            if (offset == 0x20 && len != 0 && len <= 32 && data.length >= 64 + len) {\n                bytes memory out = new bytes(len);\n                for (uint256 i; i < len; ++i) out[i] = data[64 + i];\n                return string(out);\n            }\n        }\n\n        return \"TOKEN\";\n    }\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":4127,"cache_read_input_tokens":53456,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":4127},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"1a0747da-09d0-40ee-9231-f80412a577ad","uuid":"441ec960-7d9e-4d3a-baba-28a3d6bd2d99","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:31:40.078Z","request_id":"req_011CdUTayM3bDR4bpfzcaLU9"}

There is also no owner and no way to remove or replace a listing.\n *\n *      Being in this registry is NOT an endorsement of the token. The token is arbitrary\n *      untrusted code; a malicious asset can drain the vault that holds it. Any UI on top of\n *      this must run its own allowlist/warning layer — see NOTES.md.\n */\ncontract SaveVaultFactory {\n    /// @notice asset => vault (address(0) if not listed yet)\n    mapping(address asset => SaveVault vault) public vaultFor;\n\n    /// @notice Every vault ever created, in creation order.\n    address[] public vaults;\n\n    event VaultCreated(address indexed asset, address indexed vault, address indexed creator);\n\n    error ZeroAddress();\n    error NotAContract(address asset);\n    error NotAnERC20(address asset);\n    error VaultAlreadyExists(address asset, SaveVault vault);\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Deploy the vault for `asset`.\n     * @param asset ERC-20 to save. Must be a contract exposing a working `balanceOf`.\n     * @return vault the newly deployed vault\n     */\n    function createVault(IERC20 asset) external returns (SaveVault vault) {\n        if (address(asset) == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();\n        if (address(asset).code.length == 0) revert NotAContract(address(asset));\n\n        SaveVault existing = vaultFor[address(asset)];\n        if (address(existing) != address(0)) revert VaultAlreadyExists(address(asset), existing);\n\n        // Cheapest possible smoke test that this is an ERC-20 at all. Not a safety check on\n        // the token's behaviour — just keeps obvious junk out of the registry.\n        (bool ok, bytes memory data) = address(asset).staticcall(\n            abi.encodeCall(IERC20.balanceOf, (address(this)))\n        );\n        if (!ok || data.length < 32) revert NotAnERC20(address(asset));\n\n        string memory sym = _symbol(address(asset));\n        // Reverts inside the constructor (e.g. absurd `decimals()`) bubble up and the token\n        // simply cannot be listed.\n        vault = new SaveVault(asset, string.concat(\"Save \", sym), string.concat(\"sv\", sym));\n\n        vaultFor[address(asset)] = vault;\n        vaults.push(address(vault));\n\n        emit VaultCreated(address(asset), address(vault), msg.sender);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Number of vaults created so far.\n    function vaultCount() external view returns (uint256) {\n        return vaults.length;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @dev Best-effort `symbol()` read. The token is untrusted, so this must not assume a\n     *      well-formed response: handles missing/reverting `symbol()`, the old bytes32 form\n     *      (MKR and friends), and refuses oversized strings that would only be a gas grief\n     *      and unreadable in a UI. Falls back to a generic symbol rather than blocking a\n     *      listing over cosmetics.\n     */\n    function _symbol(address token) private view returns (string memory) {\n        (bool ok, bytes memory data) = token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSignature(\"symbol()\"));\n        if (!ok) return \"TOKEN\";\n\n        if (data.length == 32) {\n            // bytes32-style symbol: take bytes up to the first zero.\n            bytes32 raw = bytes32(data);\n            uint256 len;\n            while (len < 32 && raw[len] != 0) len++;\n            if (len == 0) return \"TOKEN\";\n            bytes memory out = new bytes(len);\n            for (uint256 i; i < len; ++i) out[i] = raw[i];\n            return string(out);\n        }\n\n        // Properly encoded `string`: 32-byte offset + 32-byte length + padded data.\n        if (data.length >= 64 && data.length <= 160) {\n            uint256 offset;\n            uint256 len;\n            assembly {\n                offset := mload(add(data, 0x20))\n                len := mload(add(data, 0x40))\n            }\n            if (offset == 0x20 && len != 0 && len <= 32 && data.length >= 64 + len) {\n                bytes memory out = new bytes(len);\n                for (uint256 i; i < len; ++i) out[i] = data[64 + i];\n                return string(out);\n            }\n        }\n\n        return \"TOKEN\";\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}

SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {ERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/ERC20.sol\";\nimport {SaveVault} from \"../../src/SaveVault.sol\";\n\n/// @notice Plain ERC-20 with configurable decimals (USDC is 6, WBTC is 8, ...).\ncontract MockERC20 is ERC20 {\n    uint8 private immutable _dec;\n\n    constructor(string memory n, string memory s, uint8 d) ERC20(n, s) {\n        _dec = d;\n    }\n\n    function decimals() public view override returns (uint8) {\n        return _dec;\n    }\n\n    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {\n        _mint(to, amount);\n    }\n}\n\n/// @notice Charges a fee on every transfer — receiver gets less than `amount`.\ncontract FeeOnTransferToken is ERC20 {\n    uint256 public feeBps;\n\n    constructor(uint256 feeBps_) ERC20(\"Fee Token\", \"FEE\") {\n        feeBps = feeBps_;\n    }\n\n    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {\n        _mint(to, amount);\n    }\n\n    function _update(address from, address to, uint256 value) internal override {\n        if (from == address(0) || to == address(0) || feeBps == 0) {\n            super._update(from, to, value);\n            return;\n        }\n        uint256 fee = (value * feeBps) / 10_000;\n        super._update(from, to, value - fee);\n        super._update(from, address(0xdead), fee);\n    }\n}\n\n/// @notice Token that re-enters the vault from inside `transfer` (ERC-777-style hook).\ncontract ReentrantToken is ERC20 {\n    SaveVault public vault;\n    bool public attacking;\n\n    constructor() ERC20(\"Reentrant\", \"RE\") {}\n\n    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {\n        _mint(to, amount);\n    }\n\n    function setVault(SaveVault v) external {\n        vault = v;\n    }\n\n    function arm() external {\n        attacking = true;\n    }\n\n    function _update(address from, address to, uint256 value) internal override {\n        super._update(from, to, value);\n        if (attacking && address(vault) != address(0) && from == address(vault)) {\n            attacking = false; // one shot\n            vault.redeem(vault.balanceOf(msg.sender), msg.sender, msg.sender);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// @notice `symbol()` returns bytes32 instead of string (MKR-style).\ncontract Bytes32SymbolToken is ERC20 {\n    constructor() ERC20(\"Maker\", \"unused\") {}\n\n    function symbol() public pure override returns (string memory) {\n        revert(\"use bytes32\");\n    }\n\n    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {\n        _mint(to, amount);\n    }\n}\n\n/// @notice Minimal token whose `symbol()` reverts and whose `decimals()` is absurd.\ncontract WeirdDecimalsToken {\n    function balanceOf(address) external pure returns (uint256) {\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    function decimals() external pure returns (uint8) {\n        return 200;\n    }\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":516,"cache_read_input_tokens":61205,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":516},"output_tokens":68,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"1a0747da-09d0-40ee-9231-f80412a577ad","uuid":"c3a09d9f-79cc-49e5-a38c-42e5c49d8176","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:32:14.465Z","request_id":"req_011CdUTegvgJQW2cgqS8P81o"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdUTfkuKcp4jVDJpAc5Cp","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01EmLjev1NrLwZ9hewdSgLUr","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/security-goal-001/2026-07-28T122531Z-claude-with-skill-3/workspace/test/mocks/Tokens.sol","content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {ERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/ERC20.sol\";\nimport {SaveVault} from \"../../src/SaveVault.sol\";\n\n/// @notice Plain ERC-20 with configurable decimals (USDC is 6, WBTC is 8, ...).\ncontract MockERC20 is ERC20 {\n    uint8 private immutable _dec;\n\n    constructor(string memory n, string memory s, uint8 d) ERC20(n, s) {\n        _dec = d;\n    }\n\n    function decimals() public view override returns (uint8) {\n        return _dec;\n    }\n\n    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {\n        _mint(to, amount);\n    }\n}\n\n/// @notice Charges a fee on every transfer — receiver gets less than `amount`.\ncontract FeeOnTransferToken is ERC20 {\n    uint256 public feeBps;\n\n    constructor(uint256 feeBps_) ERC20(\"Fee Token\", \"FEE\") {\n        feeBps = feeBps_;\n    }\n\n    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {\n        _mint(to, amount);\n    }\n\n    function _update(address from, address to, uint256 value) internal override {\n        if (from == address(0) || to == address(0) || feeBps == 0) {\n            super._update(from, to, value);\n            return;\n        }\n        uint256 fee = (value * feeBps) / 10_000;\n        super._update(from, to, value - fee);\n        super._update(from, address(0xdead), fee);\n    }\n}\n\n/// @notice Token that calls back into the vault from inside `transfer` (ERC-777-style hook).\ncontract ReentrantToken is ERC20 {\n    SaveVault public vault;\n    bool public armed;\n\n    constructor() ERC20(\"Reentrant\", \"RE\") {}\n\n    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {\n        _mint(to, amount);\n    }\n\n    function setVault(SaveVault v) external {\n        vault = v;\n    }\n\n    function arm() external {\n        armed = true;\n    }\n\n    function _update(address from, address to, uint256 value) internal override {\n        super._update(from, to, value);\n        if (armed && address(vault) != address(0) && from == address(vault)) {\n            armed = false; // one shot\n            vault.sync(); // any state-changing re-entry is enough to prove the guard is live\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// @notice `symbol()` returns bytes32 instead of string (MKR-style). Not a full ERC-20.\ncontract Bytes32SymbolToken {\n    function balanceOf(address) external pure returns (uint256) {\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    function decimals() external pure returns (uint8) {\n        return 18;\n    }\n\n    function symbol() external pure returns (bytes32) {\n        return \"MKR\";\n    }\n}\n\n/// @notice No `symbol()` at all.\ncontract NoMetadataToken {\n    function balanceOf(address) external pure returns (uint256) {\n        return 0;\n    }\n}\n\n/// @notice Reports an absurd `decimals()`, which would break share math.\ncontract WeirdDecimalsToken {\n    function balanceOf(address) external pure returns (uint256) {\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    function decimals() external pure returns (uint8) {\n        return 200;\n    }\n\n    function symbol() external pure returns (string memory) {\n        return \"WEIRD\";\n    }\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1468,"cache_read_input_tokens":61721,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1468},"output_tokens":10,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"1a0747da-09d0-40ee-9231-f80412a577ad","uuid":"a72de301-c594-48c8-a572-92cff6ec844f","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:32:36.208Z","request_id":"req_011CdUTfguy83MVm1N4horBf"}

SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {Test} from \"forge-std/Test.sol\";\nimport {IERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport {IERC20Metadata} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/extensions/IERC20Metadata.sol\";\nimport {ReentrancyGuard} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol\";\n\nimport {SaveVault} from \"../src/SaveVault.sol\";\nimport {SaveVaultFactory} from \"../src/SaveVaultFactory.sol\";\nimport {\n    MockERC20,\n    FeeOnTransferToken,\n    ReentrantToken,\n    Bytes32SymbolToken,\n    NoMetadataToken,\n    WeirdDecimalsToken\n} from \"./mocks/Tokens.sol\";\n\ncontract SaveVaultTest is Test {\n    SaveVaultFactory factory;\n    MockERC20 usdc; // 6 decimals, like the real thing\n    SaveVault vault;\n\n    address alice = makeAddr(\"alice\");\n    address bob = makeAddr(\"bob\");\n    address keeper = makeAddr(\"keeper\");\n    address attacker = makeAddr(\"attacker\");\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        factory = new SaveVaultFactory();\n        usdc = new MockERC20(\"USD Coin\", \"USDC\", 6);\n        vault = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(usdc)));\n    }\n\n    function _fund(address who, uint256 amount) internal {\n        usdc.mint(who, amount);\n        vm.prank(who);\n        usdc.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n    }\n\n    function _deposit(address who, uint256 amount) internal returns (uint256 shares) {\n        _fund(who, amount);\n        vm.prank(who);\n        shares = vault.deposit(amount, who);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------- receipt token\n\n    function test_ReceiptTokenTracksAssetDecimals() public view {\n        assertEq(vault.symbol(), \"svUSDC\");\n        assertEq(vault.name(), \"Save USDC\");\n        // asset decimals (6) + virtual-share offset (3) — never a hardcoded 18\n        assertEq(vault.decimals(), 9);\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(vault.asset()).decimals(), 6);\n    }\n\n    function test_ReceiptIsTransferableAndCarriesTheClaim() public {\n        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, 1_000e6);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.transfer(bob, shares);\n\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), 0);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 out = vault.redeem(shares, bob, bob);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(out, 1_000e6, 1);\n        assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(bob), out);\n    }\n\n    function test_RoundTripNeverProfits() public {\n        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, 1_000e6);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 out = vault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n        assertLe(out, 1_000e6, \"round trip must not mint value\");\n        assertApproxEqAbs(out, 1_000e6, 1);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------- yield accounting\n\n    function test_KeeperYieldStreamsOverDripDuration() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1_000e6);\n\n        usdc.mint(keeper, 100e6);\n        vm.startPrank(keeper);\n        usdc.approve(address(vault), 100e6);\n        vault.donate(100e6);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        // Nothing lands on the share price in the keeper's own block.\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1_000e6);\n        assertEq(vault.pendingYield(), 100e6);\n\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 12 hours);\n        assertApproxEqRel(vault.totalAssets(), 1_050e6, 0.001e18);\n\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 13 hours); // past the end of the stream\n        assertApproxEqRel(vault.totalAssets(), 1_100e6, 0.001e18);\n\n        // Alice, the only holder, ends up with essentially all of it.\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 out = vault.redeem(vault.balanceOf(alice), alice, alice);\n        assertApproxEqRel(out, 1_100e6, 0.001e18);\n    }\n\n    function test_RawTransferNeedsSyncAndCannotBeSnipedEither() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1_000e6);\n\n        // Keeper forgets `donate` and just transfers in.\n        usdc.mint(address(vault), 100e6);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1_000e6, \"uncredited until synced\");\n\n        // Anyone can start the stream.\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 queued = vault.sync();\n        assertEq(queued, 100e6);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1_000e6);\n\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 1 days);\n        assertApproxEqRel(vault.totalAssets(), 1_100e6, 0.001e18);\n    }\n\n    function test_YieldSnipingIsUnprofitable() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1_000e6);\n\n        usdc.mint(keeper, 100e6);\n        vm.startPrank(keeper);\n        usdc.approve(address(vault), 100e6);\n        vault.donate(100e6);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        // Sniper deposits behind the keeper and exits in the same block.\n        _fund(attacker, 1_000e6);\n        vm.startPrank(attacker);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(1_000e6, attacker);\n        uint256 out = vault.redeem(shares, attacker, attacker);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        assertLe(out, 1_000e6, \"sniper captured yield\");\n\n        // ...and the yield still reaches the holder who was actually there.\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 1 days);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 aliceOut = vault.redeem(vault.balanceOf(alice), alice, alice);\n        assertApproxEqRel(aliceOut, 1_100e6, 0.001e18);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Classic ERC-4626 first-depositor inflation attack, run in its most favourable\n    ///      form for the attacker: donation fully vested before the victim arrives.\n    function test_InflationAttackDoesNotStealFromVictim() public {\n        _deposit(attacker, 1); // 1 wei of USDC\n\n        usdc.mint(attacker, 1_000e6);\n        vm.prank(attacker);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 1_000e6);\n        vault.sync();\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 1 days); // let the donation fully land\n\n        uint256 victimShares = _deposit(bob, 2_000e6);\n        assertGt(victimShares, 0, \"victim must not be rounded to zero shares\");\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 victimOut = vault.redeem(victimShares, bob, bob);\n        assertApproxEqRel(victimOut, 2_000e6, 0.001e18);\n\n        vm.prank(attacker);\n        uint256 attackerOut = vault.redeem(vault.balanceOf(attacker), attacker, attacker);\n        assertLt(attackerOut, 1_000e6 + 1, \"attack must not be profitable\");\n    }\n\n    function test_SyncIsNoopWhenNothingArrived() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1_000e6);\n        assertEq(vault.sync(), 0);\n        (uint256 rate,) = vault.dripState();\n        assertEq(rate, 0);\n    }\n\n    function test_DustBelowOneWeiPerSecondIsNotLost() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1_000e6);\n\n        usdc.mint(address(vault), 100); // < DRIP_DURATION, rate rounds to 0\n        vault.sync();\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 2 days);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1_000e6);\n        assertEq(vault.pendingYield(), 100);\n\n        // A later, larger sync sweeps the dust in with it.\n        usdc.mint(address(vault), 100e6);\n        vault.sync();\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 1 days);\n        assertApproxEqRel(vault.totalAssets(), 1_000e6 + 100e6 + 100, 0.001e18);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------- hostile tokens\n\n    function test_FeeOnTransferDepositReverts() public {\n        FeeOnTransferToken fee = new FeeOnTransferToken(100); // 1%\n        SaveVault feeVault = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(fee)));\n\n        fee.mint(alice, 1_000e18);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        fee.approve(address(feeVault), type(uint256).max);\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVault.AssetTransferShortfall.selector, 1_000e18, 990e18));\n        feeVault.deposit(1_000e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    function test_ReentrantAssetCannotReenter() public {\n        ReentrantToken re = new ReentrantToken();\n        SaveVault reVault = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(re)));\n        re.setVault(reVault);\n\n        re.mint(alice, 1_000e18);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        re.approve(address(reVault), type(uint256).max);\n        uint256 shares = reVault.deposit(1_000e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        re.arm();\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(ReentrancyGuard.ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall.selector);\n        reVault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------- input validation\n\n    function test_ZeroValueCallsRevert() public {\n        _fund(alice, 1_000e6);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAmount.selector);\n        vault.deposit(0, alice);\n\n        vault.deposit(1_000e6, alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAmount.selector);\n        vault.redeem(0, alice, alice);\n\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAmount.selector);\n        vault.donate(0);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    function test_WithdrawBeyondClaimReverts() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1_000e6);\n        _deposit(bob, 1_000e6);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        vault.withdraw(1_500e6, alice, alice); // more than alice's pro-rata claim\n    }\n\n    function test_ThirdPartyWithdrawNeedsAllowance() public {\n        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, 1_000e6);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        vault.redeem(shares, bob, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.approve(bob, shares);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 out = vault.redeem(shares, bob, alice);\n        assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(bob), out);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------- factory\n\n    function test_ListingIsPermissionlessAndOnePerToken() public {\n        MockERC20 dai = new MockERC20(\"Dai\", \"DAI\", 18);\n\n        vm.prank(attacker); // anyone at all\n        SaveVault v = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(dai)));\n        assertEq(address(factory.vaultFor(address(dai))), address(v));\n        assertEq(factory.vaultCount(), 2);\n\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVaultFactory.VaultAlreadyExists.selector, address(dai), v));\n        factory.createVault(IERC20(address(dai)));\n    }\n\n    function test_RejectsNonTokens() public {\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVaultFactory.ZeroAddress.selector);\n        factory.createVault(IERC20(address(0)));\n\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVaultFactory.NotAContract.selector, alice));\n        factory.createVault(IERC20(alice));\n\n        // A contract with no `balanceOf`.\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVaultFactory.NotAnERC20.selector, address(factory)));\n        factory.createVault(IERC20(address(factory)));\n    }\n\n    function test_HandlesOddMetadata() public {\n        SaveVault mkr = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(new Bytes32SymbolToken())));\n        assertEq(mkr.symbol(), \"svMKR\");\n\n        SaveVault bare = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(new NoMetadataToken())));\n        assertEq(bare.symbol(), \"svTOKEN\");\n        assertEq(bare.decimals(), 21); // 18 fallback + offset\n    }\n\n    function test_RejectsAbsurdDecimals() public {\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVault.UnsupportedDecimals.selector, 203));\n        factory.createVault(IERC20(address(new WeirdDecimalsToken())));\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------- fuzz\n\n    function testFuzz_DepositRedeemNeverMintsValue(uint256 amount, uint8 dec) public {\n        dec = uint8(bound(dec, 0, 36));\n        amount = bound(amount, 1, 1e30);\n\n        MockERC20 token = new MockERC20(\"Token\", \"TKN\", dec);\n        SaveVault v = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(token)));\n\n        token.mint(alice, amount);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        token.approve(address(v), amount);\n        uint256 shares = v.deposit(amount, alice);\n        uint256 out = v.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        assertLe(out, amount);\n    }\n\n    function testFuzz_ProRataSplitIsFair(uint256 a, uint256 b, uint256 yield_) public {\n        a = bound(a, 1e6, 1e24);\n        b = bound(b, 1e6, 1e24);\n        yield_ = bound(yield_, 0, 1e24);\n\n        _deposit(alice, a);\n        _deposit(bob, b);\n\n        usdc.mint(address(vault), yield_);\n        if (yield_ > 0) vault.sync();\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 1 days);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 aOut = vault.redeem(vault.balanceOf(alice), alice, alice);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 bOut = vault.redeem(vault.balanceOf(bob), bob, bob);\n\n        // Neither depositor can end up with more than their stake plus their share of yield.\n        assertLe(aOut + bOut, a + b + yield_);\n        // And each keeps at least their principal minus rounding.\n        assertGe(aOut + 2, a);\n        assertGe(bOut + 2, b);\n    }\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2110,"cache_read_input_tokens":63189,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2110},"output_tokens":6,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"1a0747da-09d0-40ee-9231-f80412a577ad","uuid":"49af2e5d-844f-4cec-a117-fd4d0c16499e","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:34:06.573Z","request_id":"req_011CdUThHsS4av3CKNV2J347"}
