test_ReentrantAssetCannotReenter() public {\n        ReentrantToken re = new ReentrantToken();\n        SaveVault reVault = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(re)));\n        re.setVault(reVault);\n\n        re.mint(alice, 1_000e18);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        re.approve(address(reVault), type(uint256).max);\n        uint256 shares = reVault.deposit(1_000e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        re.arm();\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(ReentrancyGuard.ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall.selector);\n        reVault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------- input validation\n\n    function test_ZeroValueCallsRevert() public {\n        _fund(alice, 1_000e6);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAmount.selector);\n        vault.deposit(0, alice);\n\n        vault.deposit(1_000e6, alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAmount.selector);\n        vault.redeem(0, alice, alice);\n\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAmount.selector);\n        vault.donate(0);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    function test_WithdrawBeyondClaimReverts() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1_000e6);\n        _deposit(bob, 1_000e6);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        vault.withdraw(1_500e6, alice, alice); // more than alice's pro-rata claim\n    }\n\n    function test_ThirdPartyWithdrawNeedsAllowance() public {\n        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, 1_000e6);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        vault.redeem(shares, bob, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.approve(bob, shares);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 out = vault.redeem(shares, bob, alice);\n        assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(bob), out);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------- factory\n\n    function test_ListingIsPermissionlessAndOnePerToken() public {\n        MockERC20 dai = new MockERC20(\"Dai\", \"DAI\", 18);\n\n        vm.prank(attacker); // anyone at all\n        SaveVault v = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(dai)));\n        assertEq(address(factory.vaultFor(address(dai))), address(v));\n        assertEq(factory.vaultCount(), 2);\n\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVaultFactory.VaultAlreadyExists.selector, address(dai), v));\n        factory.createVault(IERC20(address(dai)));\n    }\n\n    function test_RejectsNonTokens() public {\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVaultFactory.ZeroAddress.selector);\n        factory.createVault(IERC20(address(0)));\n\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVaultFactory.NotAContract.selector, alice));\n        factory.createVault(IERC20(alice));\n\n        // A contract with no `balanceOf`.\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVaultFactory.NotAnERC20.selector, address(factory)));\n        factory.createVault(IERC20(address(factory)));\n    }\n\n    function test_HandlesOddMetadata() public {\n        SaveVault mkr = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(new Bytes32SymbolToken())));\n        assertEq(mkr.symbol(), \"svMKR\");\n\n        SaveVault bare = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(new NoMetadataToken())));\n        assertEq(bare.symbol(), \"svTOKEN\");\n        assertEq(bare.decimals(), 21); // 18 fallback + offset\n    }\n\n    function test_RejectsAbsurdDecimals() public {\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVault.UnsupportedDecimals.selector, 203));\n        factory.createVault(IERC20(address(new WeirdDecimalsToken())));\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------- fuzz\n\n    function testFuzz_DepositRedeemNeverMintsValue(uint256 amount, uint8 dec) public {\n        dec = uint8(bound(dec, 0, 36));\n        amount = bound(amount, 1, 1e30);\n\n        MockERC20 token = new MockERC20(\"Token\", \"TKN\", dec);\n        SaveVault v = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(token)));\n\n        token.mint(alice, amount);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        token.approve(address(v), amount);\n        uint256 shares = v.deposit(amount, alice);\n        uint256 out = v.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        assertLe(out, amount);\n    }\n\n    function testFuzz_ProRataSplitIsFair(uint256 a, uint256 b, uint256 yield_) public {\n        a = bound(a, 1e6, 1e24);\n        b = bound(b, 1e6, 1e24);\n        yield_ = bound(yield_, 0, 1e24);\n\n        _deposit(alice, a);\n        _deposit(bob, b);\n\n        usdc.mint(address(vault), yield_);\n        if (yield_ > 0) vault.sync();\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 1 days);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 aOut = vault.redeem(vault.balanceOf(alice), alice, alice);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 bOut = vault.redeem(vault.balanceOf(bob), bob, bob);\n\n        // Neither depositor can end up with more than their stake plus their share of yield.\n        assertLe(aOut + bOut, a + b + yield_);\n        // And each keeps at least their principal minus rounding.\n        assertGe(aOut + 2, a);\n        assertGe(bOut + 2, b);\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}

Depositors get a transferable ERC-20 receipt\n *         (the vault's own shares) representing a pro-rata claim on the vault's assets.\n *         Yield is more of the same underlying token, pushed in by a keeper.\n *\n * Design decisions that matter:\n *\n * 1. No admin. No owner, no fees, no pause, no upgrade path. Listing is permissionless,\n *    so any privileged role would be a lever over other people's savings and a censorship\n *    vector on a product whose whole promise is \"withdraw whenever\". The tradeoff is real:\n *    nothing can be rescued or fixed after deployment. See NOTES.md.\n *\n * 2. Accounted assets, not `balanceOf`. `totalAssets()` is an internal number, not the\n *    token balance. Tokens that appear in the vault are not credited until someone calls\n *    `sync()` (or the keeper uses `donate()`), and are then streamed in linearly over\n *    DRIP_DURATION. This kills two attacks at once:\n *      - yield sniping: a bot cannot deposit in front of the keeper's transfer and withdraw\n *        behind it, because a lump sum never lands on the share price in one block;\n *      - atomic share-price inflation: a donation inside a single transaction moves\n *        `totalAssets()` by ~0, so the classic first-depositor sandwich has nothing to grip.\n *\n * 3. Virtual shares offset (`_decimalsOffset() == 3`) on top of that, as the standard\n *    ERC-4626 inflation-attack mitigation for the non-atomic case.\n *\n * 4. Deposits must actually deliver what they claim. `_deposit` measures the balance delta\n *    and reverts if less arrived than was priced, so fee-on-transfer tokens cannot mint\n *    shares against assets the vault never received (which would dilute existing holders).\n *\n * @dev The underlying token is untrusted by construction — anyone can list anything. Every\n *      vault holds exactly one asset and shares no state with other vaults, so a malicious\n *      or broken token can only harm depositors of its own vault. Vetting the token is a\n *      frontend/operator responsibility, not something this contract can do.\n */\ncontract SaveVault is ERC4626, ReentrancyGuard {\n    using SafeERC20 for IERC20;\n\n    /// @notice Window over which newly arrived assets are credited to the share price.\n    uint256 public constant DRIP_DURATION = 1 days;\n\n    /// @notice Largest share decimals this vault will accept (asset decimals + offset).\n    uint8 public constant MAX_SHARE_DECIMALS = 39;\n\n    /// @dev Assets credited to depositors as of `lastAccrual`.\n    uint256 private _storedAssets;\n    /// @dev Assets credited per second by the active stream.\n    uint256 private _dripRate;\n    /// @dev Timestamp the active stream stops paying out.\n    uint256 private _dripEnd;\n    /// @dev Last timestamp the stream was accounted for (may be < block.timestamp).\n    uint256 private _lastAccrual;\n\n    /// @notice Emitted when assets found in the vault are queued for streaming.\n    event YieldQueued(address indexed caller, uint256 amount, uint256 dripEnd);\n\n    error ZeroAmount();\n    error UnsupportedDecimals(uint8 shareDecimals);\n    error AssetTransferShortfall(uint256 expected, uint256 received);\n\n    /**\n     * @param asset_ underlying ERC-20\n     * @param name_ receipt token name\n     * @param symbol_ receipt token symbol\n     */\n    constructor(IERC20 asset_, string memory name_, string memory symbol_) ERC20(name_, symbol_) ERC4626(asset_) {\n        // ERC4626 falls back to 18 decimals if the asset does not expose `decimals()`.\n        // A token reporting an absurd value would make share math unusable (or overflow\n        // the uint8 in `decimals()`), so refuse to exist rather than deploy a broken vault.\n        uint8 shareDecimals = decimals();\n        if (shareDecimals > MAX_SHARE_DECIMALS) revert UnsupportedDecimals(shareDecimals);\n\n        _lastAccrual = block.timestamp;\n        _dripEnd = block.timestamp;\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- accounting\n\n    /// @inheritdoc ERC4626\n    /// @dev Credited assets only: `_storedAssets` plus the part of the active stream that\n    ///      has vested. Deliberately not `asset.balanceOf(this)` — see contract docs.\n    function totalAssets() public view override returns (uint256) {\n        return _storedAssets + _accruedYield();\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Assets sitting in the vault that are not yet part of any holder's claim:\n    ///         the unvested remainder of the active stream plus anything not yet `sync()`ed.\n    function pendingYield() public view returns (uint256) {\n        return IERC20(asset()).balanceOf(address(this)) - totalAssets();\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Current stream: assets per second and the timestamp it ends.\n    function dripState() external view returns (uint256 ratePerSecond, uint256 endsAt) {\n        return (_dripRate, _dripEnd);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Credit vested yield and start a new stream for everything that has arrived\n     *         since the last call. Permissionless and safe to call by anyone at any time:\n     *         it never moves assets and never changes the share price in the calling block.\n     * @return queued assets put into the new stream\n     */\n    function sync() external nonReentrant returns (uint256 queued) {\n        return _sync();\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Push yield in and start streaming it in one call. Preferred keeper entrypoint:\n     *         a plain `transfer` + `sync()` works too, but this cannot be forgotten halfway.\n     * @param amount assets to pull from `msg.sender`\n     * @return queued assets put into the new stream (>= amount only if untracked assets were waiting)\n     */\n    function donate(uint256 amount) external nonReentrant returns (uint256 queued) {\n        if (amount == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        IERC20(asset()).safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);\n        return _sync();\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- internals\n\n    function _accruedYield() private view returns (uint256) {\n        uint256 upTo = block.timestamp < _dripEnd ? block.timestamp : _dripEnd;\n        if (upTo <= _lastAccrual) return 0;\n        return (upTo - _lastAccrual) * _dripRate;\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Fold vested yield into `_storedAssets`. Share price is unchanged by this call:\n    ///      `totalAssets()` is continuous in time, this only moves where the number is kept.\n    function _settle() private {\n        uint256 accrued = _accruedYield();\n        if (accrued != 0) _storedAssets += accrued;\n\n        uint256 upTo = block.timestamp < _dripEnd ? block.timestamp : _dripEnd;\n        if (upTo > _lastAccrual) _lastAccrual = upTo;\n    }\n\n    function _sync() private returns (uint256 queued) {\n        _settle();\n\n        // Everything in the vault that is not yet credited: the unvested tail of the old\n        // stream plus any new arrivals. Balance-based, so fee-on-transfer and rebase-up\n        // tokens are handled by construction — only what really showed up gets streamed.\n        queued = IERC20(asset()).balanceOf(address(this)) - _storedAssets;\n        if (queued == 0) return 0;\n\n        // Integer division leaves < DRIP_DURATION wei of dust uncredited; it is picked up\n        // by the next `sync()`, never lost.\n        _dripRate = queued / DRIP_DURATION;\n        _lastAccrual = block.timestamp;\n        _dripEnd = block.timestamp + DRIP_DURATION;\n\n        emit YieldQueued(msg.sender, queued, _dripEnd);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Standard ERC-4626 inflation-attack mitigation: 1e3 virtual shares against 1 virtual asset.\n    function _decimalsOffset() internal pure override returns (uint8) {\n        return 3;\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- 4626 hooks\n\n    /**\n     * @dev Shares were priced off `totalAssets()` before this call, so the transfer must\n     *      deliver at least `assets` or the mint would be backed by nothing. Reverting\n     *      (rather than crediting the delta) keeps `deposit`/`mint` exactly as\n     *      `previewDeposit`/`previewMint` advertised them.\n     */\n    function _deposit(address caller, address receiver, uint256 assets, uint256 shares)\n        internal\n        override\n        nonReentrant\n    {\n        if (assets == 0 || shares == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n\n        _settle();\n\n        IERC20 token = IERC20(asset());\n        uint256 balanceBefore = token.balanceOf(address(this));\n        token.safeTransferFrom(caller, address(this), assets);\n        uint256 received = token.balanceOf(address(this)) - balanceBefore;\n        if (received < assets) revert AssetTransferShortfall(assets, received);\n\n        // Credit exactly what the shares were priced on. Any surplus stays uncredited\n        // until `sync()` streams it, instead of being a gift to the depositor's own shares.\n        _storedAssets += assets;\n        _mint(receiver, shares);\n\n        emit Deposit(caller, receiver, assets, shares);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Checks-effects-interactions: allowance spent and shares burned before the transfer out.\n    function _withdraw(address caller, address receiver, address owner, uint256 assets, uint256 shares)\n        internal\n        override\n        nonReentrant\n    {\n        if (assets == 0 || shares == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n\n        _settle();\n\n        if (caller != owner) _spendAllowance(owner, caller, shares);\n\n        _burn(owner, shares);\n        _storedAssets -= assets;\n        IERC20(asset()).safeTransfer(receiver, assets);\n\n        emit Withdraw(caller, receiver, owner, assets, shares);\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":47,"oldLines":8,"newStart":47,"newLines":8,"lines":["     /// @notice Window over which newly arrived assets are credited to the share price.","     uint256 public constant DRIP_DURATION = 1 days;"," ","-    /// @notice Largest share decimals this vault will accept (asset decimals + offset).","-    uint8 public constant MAX_SHARE_DECIMALS = 39;","+    /// @notice Largest asset decimals this vault will accept.","+    uint256 public constant MAX_ASSET_DECIMALS = 36;"," ","     /// @dev Assets credited to depositors as of `lastAccrual`.","     uint256 private _storedAssets;"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false}}

Depositors get a transferable ERC-20 receipt\n *         (the vault's own shares) representing a pro-rata claim on the vault's assets.\n *         Yield is more of the same underlying token, pushed in by a keeper.\n *\n * Design decisions that matter:\n *\n * 1. No admin. No owner, no fees, no pause, no upgrade path. Listing is permissionless,\n *    so any privileged role would be a lever over other people's savings and a censorship\n *    vector on a product whose whole promise is \"withdraw whenever\". The tradeoff is real:\n *    nothing can be rescued or fixed after deployment. See NOTES.md.\n *\n * 2. Accounted assets, not `balanceOf`. `totalAssets()` is an internal number, not the\n *    token balance. Tokens that appear in the vault are not credited until someone calls\n *    `sync()` (or the keeper uses `donate()`), and are then streamed in linearly over\n *    DRIP_DURATION. This kills two attacks at once:\n *      - yield sniping: a bot cannot deposit in front of the keeper's transfer and withdraw\n *        behind it, because a lump sum never lands on the share price in one block;\n *      - atomic share-price inflation: a donation inside a single transaction moves\n *        `totalAssets()` by ~0, so the classic first-depositor sandwich has nothing to grip.\n *\n * 3. Virtual shares offset (`_decimalsOffset() == 3`) on top of that, as the standard\n *    ERC-4626 inflation-attack mitigation for the non-atomic case.\n *\n * 4. Deposits must actually deliver what they claim. `_deposit` measures the balance delta\n *    and reverts if less arrived than was priced, so fee-on-transfer tokens cannot mint\n *    shares against assets the vault never received (which would dilute existing holders).\n *\n * @dev The underlying token is untrusted by construction — anyone can list anything. Every\n *      vault holds exactly one asset and shares no state with other vaults, so a malicious\n *      or broken token can only harm depositors of its own vault. Vetting the token is a\n *      frontend/operator responsibility, not something this contract can do.\n */\ncontract SaveVault is ERC4626, ReentrancyGuard {\n    using SafeERC20 for IERC20;\n\n    /// @notice Window over which newly arrived assets are credited to the share price.\n    uint256 public constant DRIP_DURATION = 1 days;\n\n    /// @notice Largest asset decimals this vault will accept.\n    uint256 public constant MAX_ASSET_DECIMALS = 36;\n\n    /// @dev Assets credited to depositors as of `lastAccrual`.\n    uint256 private _storedAssets;\n    /// @dev Assets credited per second by the active stream.\n    uint256 private _dripRate;\n    /// @dev Timestamp the active stream stops paying out.\n    uint256 private _dripEnd;\n    /// @dev Last timestamp the stream was accounted for (may be < block.timestamp).\n    uint256 private _lastAccrual;\n\n    /// @notice Emitted when assets found in the vault are queued for streaming.\n    event YieldQueued(address indexed caller, uint256 amount, uint256 dripEnd);\n\n    error ZeroAmount();\n    error UnsupportedDecimals(uint256 assetDecimals);\n    error AssetTransferShortfall(uint256 expected, uint256 received);\n\n    /**\n     * @param asset_ underlying ERC-20\n     * @param name_ receipt token name\n     * @param symbol_ receipt token symbol\n     */\n    constructor(IERC20 asset_, string memory name_, string memory symbol_) ERC20(name_, symbol_) ERC4626(asset_) {\n        // ERC4626 falls back to 18 decimals if the asset does not expose `decimals()`.\n        // A token reporting an absurd value would make share math unusable (or overflow\n        // the uint8 in `decimals()`), so refuse to exist rather than deploy a broken vault.\n        uint8 shareDecimals = decimals();\n        if (shareDecimals > MAX_SHARE_DECIMALS) revert UnsupportedDecimals(shareDecimals);\n\n        _lastAccrual = block.timestamp;\n        _dripEnd = block.timestamp;\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- accounting\n\n    /// @inheritdoc ERC4626\n    /// @dev Credited assets only: `_storedAssets` plus the part of the active stream that\n    ///      has vested. Deliberately not `asset.balanceOf(this)` — see contract docs.\n    function totalAssets() public view override returns (uint256) {\n        return _storedAssets + _accruedYield();\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Assets sitting in the vault that are not yet part of any holder's claim:\n    ///         the unvested remainder of the active stream plus anything not yet `sync()`ed.\n    function pendingYield() public view returns (uint256) {\n        return IERC20(asset()).balanceOf(address(this)) - totalAssets();\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Current stream: assets per second and the timestamp it ends.\n    function dripState() external view returns (uint256 ratePerSecond, uint256 endsAt) {\n        return (_dripRate, _dripEnd);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Credit vested yield and start a new stream for everything that has arrived\n     *         since the last call. Permissionless and safe to call by anyone at any time:\n     *         it never moves assets and never changes the share price in the calling block.\n     * @return queued assets put into the new stream\n     */\n    function sync() external nonReentrant returns (uint256 queued) {\n        return _sync();\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Push yield in and start streaming it in one call. Preferred keeper entrypoint:\n     *         a plain `transfer` + `sync()` works too, but this cannot be forgotten halfway.\n     * @param amount assets to pull from `msg.sender`\n     * @return queued assets put into the new stream (>= amount only if untracked assets were waiting)\n     */\n    function donate(uint256 amount) external nonReentrant returns (uint256 queued) {\n        if (amount == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n        IERC20(asset()).safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);\n        return _sync();\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- internals\n\n    function _accruedYield() private view returns (uint256) {\n        uint256 upTo = block.timestamp < _dripEnd ? block.timestamp : _dripEnd;\n        if (upTo <= _lastAccrual) return 0;\n        return (upTo - _lastAccrual) * _dripRate;\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Fold vested yield into `_storedAssets`. Share price is unchanged by this call:\n    ///      `totalAssets()` is continuous in time, this only moves where the number is kept.\n    function _settle() private {\n        uint256 accrued = _accruedYield();\n        if (accrued != 0) _storedAssets += accrued;\n\n        uint256 upTo = block.timestamp < _dripEnd ? block.timestamp : _dripEnd;\n        if (upTo > _lastAccrual) _lastAccrual = upTo;\n    }\n\n    function _sync() private returns (uint256 queued) {\n        _settle();\n\n        // Everything in the vault that is not yet credited: the unvested tail of the old\n        // stream plus any new arrivals. Balance-based, so fee-on-transfer and rebase-up\n        // tokens are handled by construction — only what really showed up gets streamed.\n        queued = IERC20(asset()).balanceOf(address(this)) - _storedAssets;\n        if (queued == 0) return 0;\n\n        // Integer division leaves < DRIP_DURATION wei of dust uncredited; it is picked up\n        // by the next `sync()`, never lost.\n        _dripRate = queued / DRIP_DURATION;\n        _lastAccrual = block.timestamp;\n        _dripEnd = block.timestamp + DRIP_DURATION;\n\n        emit YieldQueued(msg.sender, queued, _dripEnd);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Standard ERC-4626 inflation-attack mitigation: 1e3 virtual shares against 1 virtual asset.\n    function _decimalsOffset() internal pure override returns (uint8) {\n        return 3;\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- 4626 hooks\n\n    /**\n     * @dev Shares were priced off `totalAssets()` before this call, so the transfer must\n     *      deliver at least `assets` or the mint would be backed by nothing. Reverting\n     *      (rather than crediting the delta) keeps `deposit`/`mint` exactly as\n     *      `previewDeposit`/`previewMint` advertised them.\n     */\n    function _deposit(address caller, address receiver, uint256 assets, uint256 shares)\n        internal\n        override\n        nonReentrant\n    {\n        if (assets == 0 || shares == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n\n        _settle();\n\n        IERC20 token = IERC20(asset());\n        uint256 balanceBefore = token.balanceOf(address(this));\n        token.safeTransferFrom(caller, address(this), assets);\n        uint256 received = token.balanceOf(address(this)) - balanceBefore;\n        if (received < assets) revert AssetTransferShortfall(assets, received);\n\n        // Credit exactly what the shares were priced on. SaveVault vault;\n\n    address alice = makeAddr(\"alice\");\n    address bob = makeAddr(\"bob\");\n    address keeper = makeAddr(\"keeper\");\n    address attacker = makeAddr(\"attacker\");\n\n  function _fund(address who, uint256 amount) internal {\n        usdc.mint(who, amount);\n        vm.prank(who);\n        usdc.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n    }\n\n    function assertEq(vault.name(), \"Save USDC\");\n        // asset decimals (6) + virtual-share offset (3) — never a hardcoded 18\n        assertEq(vault.decimals(), 9);\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(vault.asset()).decimals(), 6);\n    }\n\n    function test_ReceiptIsTransferableAndCarriesTheClaim() public {\n        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, 1_000e6);\n\n assertApproxEqAbs(out, 1_000e6, 1);\n        assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(bob), out);\n    }\n\n    function test_RoundTripNeverProfits() public {\n        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, 1_000e6);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 out = vault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n        assertLe(out, 1_000e6, \"round trip must not mint value\");\n        assertApproxEqAbs(out, 1_000e6, 1);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------- yield accounting\n\n    function test_KeeperYieldStreamsOverDripDuration() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1_000e6);\n\n        usdc.mint(keeper, 100e6);\n        vm.startPrank(keeper);\n        usdc.approve(address(vault), 100e6);\n        vault.donate(100e6);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        // Nothing lands on the share price in the keeper's own block.\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1_000e6);\n        assertEq(vault.pendingYield(), 100e6);\n\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 12 hours);\n        assertApproxEqRel(vault.totalAssets(), 1_050e6, 0.001e18);\n\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 13 hours); // past the end of the stream\n        assertApproxEqRel(vault.totalAssets(), 1_100e6, 0.001e18);\n\n        // Alice, the only holder, ends up with essentially all of it.\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 out = vault.redeem(vault.balanceOf(alice), alice, alice);\n        assertApproxEqRel(out, 1_100e6, 0.001e18);\n    }\n\n    function test_RawTransferNeedsSyncAndCannotBeSnipedEither() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1_000e6);\n\n        // Keeper forgets `donate` vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 queued = vault.sync();\n        assertEq(queued, 100e6);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1_000e6);\n\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 1 days);\n // deploy first: expectRevert binds to the next call\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVault.UnsupportedDecimals.selector, 200));\n        factory.createVault(IERC20(weird));","originalFile":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {Test} from \"forge-std/Test.sol\";\nimport {IERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport {IERC20Metadata} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/extensions/IERC20Metadata.sol\";\nimport {ReentrancyGuard} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/ReentrancyGuard.sol\";\n\nimport {SaveVault} from \"../src/SaveVault.sol\";\nimport {SaveVaultFactory} from \"../src/SaveVaultFactory.sol\";\nimport {\n    MockERC20,\n    FeeOnTransferToken,\n    ReentrantToken,\n    Bytes32SymbolToken,\n    NoMetadataToken,\n    WeirdDecimalsToken\n} from \"./mocks/Tokens.sol\";\n\ncontract SaveVaultTest is Test {\n    SaveVaultFactory factory;\n    MockERC20 usdc; // 6 decimals, like the real thing\n    SaveVault vault;\n\n    address alice = makeAddr(\"alice\");\n    address bob = makeAddr(\"bob\");\n    address keeper = makeAddr(\"keeper\");\n    address attacker = makeAddr(\"attacker\");\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        factory = new SaveVaultFactory();\n        usdc = new MockERC20(\"USD Coin\", \"USDC\", 6);\n        vault = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(usdc)));\n    }\n\n    function _fund(address who, uint256 amount) internal {\n        usdc.mint(who, amount);\n        vm.prank(who);\n        usdc.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n    }\n\n    function _deposit(address who, uint256 amount) internal returns (uint256 shares) {\n        _fund(who, amount);\n        vm.prank(who);\n        shares = vault.deposit(amount, who);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Redeem everything `who` holds. Reads the balance before pranking on purpose —\n    ///      an inline `vault.balanceOf(who)` argument would consume the prank.\n    function _redeemAll(address who) internal returns (uint256 assets) {\n        uint256 shares = vault.balanceOf(who);\n        vm.prank(who);\n        assets = vault.redeem(shares, who, who);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------- receipt token\n\n    function test_ReceiptTokenTracksAssetDecimals() public view {\n        assertEq(vault.symbol(), \"svUSDC\");\n        assertEq(vault.name(), \"Save USDC\");\n        // asset decimals (6) + virtual-share offset (3) — never a hardcoded 18\n        assertEq(vault.decimals(), 9);\n        assertEq(IERC20Metadata(vault.asset()).decimals(), 6);\n    }\n\n    function test_ReceiptIsTransferableAndCarriesTheClaim() public {\n        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, 1_000e6);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.transfer(bob, shares);\n\n        assertEq(vault.balanceOf(alice), 0);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 out = vault.redeem(shares, bob, bob);\n        assertApproxEqAbs(out, 1_000e6, 1);\n        assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(bob), out);\n    }\n\n    function test_RoundTripNeverProfits() public {\n        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, 1_000e6);\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 out = vault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n        assertLe(out, 1_000e6, \"round trip must not mint value\");\n        assertApproxEqAbs(out, 1_000e6, 1);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------- yield accounting\n\n    function test_KeeperYieldStreamsOverDripDuration() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1_000e6);\n\n        usdc.mint(keeper, 100e6);\n        vm.startPrank(keeper);\n        usdc.approve(address(vault), 100e6);\n        vault.donate(100e6);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        // Nothing lands on the share price in the keeper's own block.\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1_000e6);\n        assertEq(vault.pendingYield(), 100e6);\n\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 12 hours);\n        assertApproxEqRel(vault.totalAssets(), 1_050e6, 0.001e18);\n\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 13 hours); // past the end of the stream\n        assertApproxEqRel(vault.totalAssets(), 1_100e6, 0.001e18);\n\n        // Alice, the only holder, ends up with essentially all of it.\n        uint256 out = _redeemAll(alice);\n        assertApproxEqRel(out, 1_100e6, 0.001e18);\n    }\n\n    function test_RawTransferNeedsSyncAndCannotBeSnipedEither() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1_000e6);\n\n        // Keeper forgets `donate` and just transfers in.\n        usdc.mint(address(vault), 100e6);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1_000e6, \"uncredited until synced\");\n\n        // Anyone can start the stream.\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 queued = vault.sync();\n        assertEq(queued, 100e6);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1_000e6);\n\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 1 days);\n        assertApproxEqRel(vault.totalAssets(), 1_100e6, 0.001e18);\n    }\n\n    function test_YieldSnipingIsUnprofitable() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1_000e6);\n\n        usdc.mint(keeper, 100e6);\n        vm.startPrank(keeper);\n        usdc.approve(address(vault), 100e6);\n        vault.donate(100e6);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        // Sniper deposits behind the keeper and exits in the same block.\n        _fund(attacker, 1_000e6);\n        vm.startPrank(attacker);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(1_000e6, attacker);\n        uint256 out = vault.redeem(shares, attacker, attacker);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        assertLe(out, 1_000e6, \"sniper captured yield\");\n\n        // ...and the yield still reaches the holder who was actually there.\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 1 days);\n        uint256 aliceOut = _redeemAll(alice);\n        assertApproxEqRel(aliceOut, 1_100e6, 0.001e18);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Classic ERC-4626 first-depositor inflation attack, run in its most favourable\n    ///      form for the attacker: donation fully vested before the victim arrives.\n    function test_InflationAttackDoesNotStealFromVictim() public {\n        _deposit(attacker, 1); // 1 wei of USDC\n\n        usdc.mint(attacker, 1_000e6);\n        vm.prank(attacker);\n        usdc.transfer(address(vault), 1_000e6);\n        vault.sync();\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 1 days); // let the donation fully land\n\n        uint256 victimShares = _deposit(bob, 2_000e6);\n        assertGt(victimShares, 0, \"victim must not be rounded to zero shares\");\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 victimOut = vault.redeem(victimShares, bob, bob);\n        assertApproxEqRel(victimOut, 2_000e6, 0.001e18);\n\n        uint256 attackerOut = _redeemAll(attacker);\n        assertLt(attackerOut, 1_000e6 + 1, \"attack must not be profitable\");\n    }\n\n    function test_SyncIsNoopWhenNothingArrived() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1_000e6);\n        assertEq(vault.sync(), 0);\n        (uint256 rate,) = vault.dripState();\n        assertEq(rate, 0);\n    }\n\n    function test_DustBelowOneWeiPerSecondIsNotLost() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1_000e6);\n\n        usdc.mint(address(vault), 100); // < DRIP_DURATION, rate rounds to 0\n        vault.sync();\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 2 days);\n        assertEq(vault.totalAssets(), 1_000e6);\n        assertEq(vault.pendingYield(), 100);\n\n        // A later, larger sync sweeps the dust in with it.\n        usdc.mint(address(vault), 100e6);\n        vault.sync();\n        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 1 days);\n        assertApproxEqRel(vault.totalAssets(), 1_000e6 + 100e6 + 100, 0.001e18);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------- hostile tokens\n\n    function test_FeeOnTransferDepositReverts() public {\n        FeeOnTransferToken fee = new FeeOnTransferToken(100); // 1%\n        SaveVault feeVault = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(fee)));\n\n        fee.mint(alice, 1_000e18);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        fee.approve(address(feeVault), type(uint256).max);\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVault.AssetTransferShortfall.selector, 1_000e18, 990e18));\n        feeVault.deposit(1_000e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    function test_ReentrantAssetCannotReenter() public {\n        ReentrantToken re = new ReentrantToken();\n        SaveVault reVault = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(re)));\n        re.setVault(reVault);\n\n        re.mint(alice, 1_000e18);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        re.approve(address(reVault), type(uint256).max);\n        uint256 shares = reVault.deposit(1_000e18, alice);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        re.arm();\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(ReentrancyGuard.ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall.selector);\n        reVault.redeem(shares, alice, alice);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------- input validation\n\n    function test_ZeroValueCallsRevert() public {\n        _fund(alice, 1_000e6);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAmount.selector);\n        vault.deposit(0, alice);\n\n        vault.deposit(1_000e6, alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAmount.selector);\n        vault.redeem(0, alice, alice);\n\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVault.ZeroAmount.selector);\n        vault.donate(0);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    function test_WithdrawBeyondClaimReverts() public {\n        _deposit(alice, 1_000e6);\n        _deposit(bob, 1_000e6);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        vault.withdraw(1_500e6, alice, alice); // more than alice's pro-rata claim\n    }\n\n    function test_ThirdPartyWithdrawNeedsAllowance() public {\n        uint256 shares = _deposit(alice, 1_000e6);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        vault.redeem(shares, bob, alice);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.approve(bob, shares);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 out = vault.redeem(shares, bob, alice);\n        assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(bob), out);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------- factory\n\n    function test_ListingIsPermissionlessAndOnePerToken() public {\n        MockERC20 dai = new MockERC20(\"Dai\", \"DAI\", 18);\n\n        vm.prank(attacker); // anyone at all\n        SaveVault v = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(dai)));\n        assertEq(address(factory.vaultFor(address(dai))), address(v));\n        assertEq(factory.vaultCount(), 2);\n\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVaultFactory.VaultAlreadyExists.selector, address(dai), v));\n        factory.createVault(IERC20(address(dai)));\n    }\n\n    function test_RejectsNonTokens() public {\n        vm.expectRevert(SaveVaultFactory.ZeroAddress.selector);\n        factory.createVault(IERC20(address(0)));\n\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVaultFactory.NotAContract.selector, alice));\n        factory.createVault(IERC20(alice));\n\n        // A contract with no `balanceOf`.\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVaultFactory.NotAnERC20.selector, address(factory)));\n        factory.createVault(IERC20(address(factory)));\n    }\n\n    function test_HandlesOddMetadata() public {\n        SaveVault mkr = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(new Bytes32SymbolToken())));\n        assertEq(mkr.symbol(), \"svMKR\");\n\n        SaveVault bare = factory.createVault(IERC20(address(new NoMetadataToken())));\n        assertEq(bare.symbol(), \"svTOKEN\");\n        assertEq(bare.decimals(), 21); // 18 fallback + offset\n    }\n\n    function test_RejectsAbsurdDecimals() public {\n        vm.expectRevert(abi.encodeWithSelector(SaveVault.UnsupportedDecimals.selector, 203));\n        factory.createVault(IERC20(address(new WeirdDecimalsToken())));\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------- fuzz\n\n    function testFuzz_DepositRedeemNeverMintsValue(uint256 amount, uint8 dec) public {\n factory.createVault(IERC20(address(token)));\n\n        token.mint(alice, amount);\n        vm.startPrank(alice);\n        token.approve(address(v), amount);\n        uint256 shares = Now NOTES.md:"}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":6241,"cache_read_input_tokens":90394,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":6241},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"1a0747da-09d0-40ee-9231-f80412a577ad","uuid":"9930c8e1-4dd7-40b5-80de-7c0e2e676f5d","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:36:23.334Z","request_id":"req_011CdUTxZziG3UR2epVS56w2"}
{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdUTxg2cJiv7vRJi5uALb","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_015F7Qk9bku4RrpSkJ53HQw1","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/security-goal-001/2026-07-28T122531Z-claude-with-skill-3/workspace/NOTES.md","content":"# SaveVault — operator notes\n\nTwo contracts:\n\n- `src/SaveVaultFactory.sol` — permissionless registry. `createVault(token)` deploys the one\n  vault for that token. No owner, no parameters, no delisting.\n- `src/SaveVault.sol` — one vault per ERC-20. ERC-4626 (OpenZeppelin v5) with three\n  deliberate deviations, all described below. No owner, no fees, no pause, no upgrade path.\n\n```bash\nforge build\nforge test -vv\nforge script script/Deploy.s.sol --rpc-url $RPC --broadcast --verify   # factory only\n```\n\n---\n\n## 1. How a depositor's claim is computed\n\nThe receipt token **is** the vault's ERC-20 share token. Holding shares is the claim; there is\nno per-address bookkeeping and no snapshot. Transferring the receipt transfers the claim, which\nis why yield can never be \"credited to an address\" — it can only move the share price.\n\nLet `S = totalSupply()` (shares) and `A = totalAssets()` (credited assets, §2).\n\n```\nshares out on deposit   = assets * (S + 1e3) / (A + 1)        rounded down\nassets out on redeem    = shares * (A + 1)   / (S + 1e3)      rounded down\n```\n\n`+1e3` / `+1` are virtual shares and a virtual asset (OZ's `_decimalsOffset() == 3`). They are\nthe standard ERC-4626 inflation-attack mitigation: with them, the first depositor cannot make\none share worth so much that the second depositor's shares round to zero. Consequences to know:\n\n- **Receipt decimals = asset decimals + 3.** A USDC vault's receipt has 9 decimals, a WBTC\n  vault's has 11, a DAI vault's has 21. Nothing anywhere assumes 18 — the vault reads the\n  asset's `decimals()` and refuses to deploy if the asset reports more than 36.\n- The initial share price is 1 asset = 1000 shares, not 1:1. Any UI or integrator must use\n  `convertToAssets` / `convertToShares` rather than assuming parity.\n- **Rounding always favours the vault**, i.e. the other depositors. Deposits round shares down,\n  `previewWithdraw` rounds shares up. A deposit-then-immediately-redeem round trip returns at\n  most what went in (usually 1 wei less). This is enforced by\n  `testFuzz_DepositRedeemNeverMintsValue`.\n- Deposits or redemptions that would round to **zero** shares or zero assets revert\n  (`ZeroAmount`) instead of silently taking the dust.\n\nYield lifts every holder's claim because it raises `A` without minting shares. Nobody has to\nclaim anything; withdrawing is the only action.\n\n## 2. `totalAssets()` is accounted, not `balanceOf`\n\nThis is the one design decision worth understanding before touching anything:\n\n```\ntotalAssets() = _storedAssets + (elapsed since last accrual) * _dripRate\npendingYield() = asset.balanceOf(vault) - totalAssets()\n```\n\nTokens sitting in the vault are **not** part of anyone's claim until someone calls `sync()`\n(or the keeper calls `donate()`), and then they are credited **linearly over\n`DRIP_DURATION = 1 days`**, not instantly.\n\nWhy, given the keeper just pushes tokens in:\n\n- **Yield sniping.** With `totalAssets() == balanceOf`, a keeper transfer of yield is a\n  step change in the share price sitting in the public mempool. A bot deposits in front of it,\n  withdraws behind it, and takes a cut of yield it was never exposed to — this is the standard\n  MEV attack on donation-based vaults, and with open withdrawals and no lockup there is nothing\n  else stopping it. Streaming means no lump sum ever lands inside one block, so there is no\n  step to sandwich (`test_YieldSnipingIsUnprofitable`).\n- **Atomic share-price inflation.** A donation made inside a single transaction moves\n  `totalAssets()` by ~0, so the classic first-depositor attack cannot be executed atomically at\n  all. The virtual offset then covers the slow version (`test_InflationAttackDoesNotStealFromVictim`).\n- **Read-only reentrancy.** Because the share price never reads the token balance, an\n  integrator that queries the vault from inside a token-transfer callback still sees a\n  consistent price.\n\nAccepted consequences, in decreasing order of how much they matter:\n\n- Yield that is streaming is shared with anyone who deposits before the stream ends. A large\n  depositor arriving right after a keeper run earns a pro-rata slice of the remaining stream.\n  This is a one-day smear rather than a one-block theft; shortening `DRIP_DURATION` makes\n  sniping easier, lengthening it dilutes short-term depositors more. One day was chosen against\n  a keeper cadence of roughly a day or less.\n- Anyone can call `sync()`, and each call restarts the stream clock for whatever is unvested.\n  Spamming it slightly delays the tail of a stream; it cannot destroy or redirect assets, and it\n  costs the spammer gas. Not worth defending against.\n- If yield is smaller than `DRIP_DURATION` in wei, the per-second rate truncates to 0 and it\n  stays in `pendingYield()` until a later, larger `sync()` sweeps it in. Dust is deferred, never\n  lost (`test_DustBelowOneWeiPerSecondIsNotLost`).\n- If every share is redeemed while a stream is running, the unvested remainder belongs to\n  whoever deposits next.\n\n## 3. Deviations from plain ERC-4626\n\n1. `totalAssets()` is the accounted number above, not the token balance.\n2. `deposit`/`mint` measure the actual balance delta and revert with `AssetTransferShortfall`\n   if less arrived than was priced. So a **fee-on-transfer token's vault simply doesn't accept\n   deposits** — deliberately, because the alternative is minting shares against assets the\n   vault never received, which dilutes everyone already in it (`test_FeeOnTransferDepositReverts`).\n3. Zero-value deposits/redemptions revert rather than no-op.\n\nEverything else — `previewDeposit`, `maxWithdraw`, allowance-based third-party withdrawals,\nthe `Deposit`/`Withdraw` events — is stock OZ behaviour. `nonReentrant` guards every path that\ntouches the asset, on top of checks-effects-interactions ordering (allowance spent and shares\nburned before assets leave).\n\n## 4. Listing a token: what the operator has to get right\n\nThe contracts cannot vet the asset, and the factory deliberately doesn't try. **Being listed is\nnot an endorsement.** The token is arbitrary untrusted code that the vault must hold, so the\nreal safety layer is the frontend allowlist, not the chain. Per token, before it is surfaced\nin any UI:\n\n- **Is the token itself trustworthy?** An upgradeable, mintable, or admin-controlled token can\n  drain, freeze, or inflate its own vault at any time and no vault design can prevent it. This\n  is the single biggest risk in a permissionless listing product. Each vault holds exactly one\n  asset and shares no state with the others, so the blast radius is that token's depositors —\n  keep it that way by never adding cross-vault logic.\n- **Fee-on-transfer?** Deposits revert (§3). Note that a token with a *switchable* fee (USDT\n  has the switch) can turn a working vault into a deposit-blocked one, and existing depositors\n  would then receive slightly less than `withdraw(assets)` asked for. Don't list these.\n- **Rebasing?** Rebase-up is safe (the surplus shows up as `pendingYield` and streams to\n  holders). **Rebase-down is not supported**: the vault's accounted assets would exceed its\n  balance and the last withdrawers would find the vault short. Use the wrapped version\n  (wstETH, not stETH).\n- **Blocklist / pausable?** USDC, USDT and friends can block an address or halt transfers.\n  Deposits and withdrawals then revert until unblocked. Acceptable, but say so in the UI.\n- **Decimals.** Read automatically; over 36 the vault refuses to deploy (`UnsupportedDecimals`).\n  Tokens with no `decimals()` are treated as 18. A token with a bytes32 `symbol()` (MKR) or a\n  missing one gets a `svTOKEN` fallback name — cosmetic only.\n- **Weird ERC-20s to just say no to:** rebasing-down, ERC-777 with hooks (the reentrancy guard\n  makes their vaults DoS-prone rather than exploitable — see `test_ReentrantAssetCannotReenter`),\n  tokens with transfer hooks that can revert selectively, and anything where `balanceOf` is not\n  monotonic under the vault's own actions.\n- **Warn about first-depositor economics** if a vault is empty: the offset makes the inflation\n  attack unprofitable, but a brand-new vault with a dust deposit is still a bad place to be the\n  second depositor at scale. Seeding a small amount at listing is the cheap fix.\n\n## 5. Running the keeper\n\n- **Use `donate(amount)`, not a raw `transfer`.** It pulls the tokens and starts the stream in\n  one transaction, so yield can never sit in the vault uncredited because a second call was\n  dropped. Approve exactly `amount` (or a small multiple of one run's size) — never\n  `type(uint256).max` from a hot keeper key.\n- If yield does arrive by plain transfer, **someone must call `sync()`** or it stays in\n  `pendingYield()` forever, invisible to the share price. `sync()` is permissionless, so\n  anyone (including a depositor) can rescue the situation, but don't rely on that: monitor\n  `pendingYield()` and alert if it is non-zero with no active stream (`dripState()`).\n- **Cadence should be ≥ `DRIP_DURATION` apart, or at least regular.** Syncing more often than\n  the stream length keeps restarting the tail, which slows distribution slightly. Roughly daily\n  runs match the 1-day window.\n- **A donate of 0 reverts**; skip the run instead of sending an empty transaction.\n- Keeper transactions are worth sending through a private mempool (Flashbots Protect). The\n  drip removes the profitable sandwich, but there is no reason to advertise the transfers.\n- The keeper key has **no privileges** — it cannot withdraw, pause, or change anything. A\n  compromised keeper key can donate tokens and nothing else. No owner, no parameters, no delisting.\n- `src/SaveVault.sol` — one vault per ERC-20. ERC-4626 (OpenZeppelin v5) with three\n  deliberate deviations, all described below. No owner, no fees, no pause, no upgrade path.\n\n```bash\nforge build\nforge test -vv\nforge script script/Deploy.s.sol --rpc-url $RPC --broadcast --verify   # factory only\n```\n\n---\n\n## 1. How a depositor's claim is computed\n\nThe receipt token **is** the vault's ERC-20 share token. Holding shares is the claim; there is\nno per-address bookkeeping and no snapshot. Transferring the receipt transfers the claim, which\nis why yield can never be \"credited to an address\" — it can only move the share price.\n\nLet `S = totalSupply()` (shares) and `A = totalAssets()` (credited assets, §2).\n\n```\nshares out on deposit   = assets * (S + 1e3) / (A + 1)        rounded down\nassets out on redeem    = shares * (A + 1)   / (S + 1e3)      rounded down\n```\n\n`+1e3` / `+1` are virtual shares and a virtual asset (OZ's `_decimalsOffset() == 3`). They are\nthe standard ERC-4626 inflation-attack mitigation: with them, the first depositor cannot make\none share worth so much that the second depositor's shares round to zero. Consequences to know:\n\n- **Receipt decimals = asset decimals + 3.** A USDC vault's receipt has 9 decimals, a WBTC\n  vault's has 11, a DAI vault's has 21. Nothing anywhere assumes 18 — the vault reads the\n  asset's `decimals()` and refuses to deploy if the asset reports more than 36.\n- The initial share price is 1 asset = 1000 shares, not 1:1. Any UI or integrator must use\n  `convertToAssets` / `convertToShares` rather than assuming parity.\n- **Rounding always favours the vault**, i.e. the other depositors. Deposits round shares down,\n  `previewWithdraw` rounds shares up. A deposit-then-immediately-redeem round trip returns at\n  most what went in (usually 1 wei less). This is enforced by\n  `testFuzz_DepositRedeemNeverMintsValue`.\n- Deposits or redemptions that would round to **zero** shares or zero assets revert\n  (`ZeroAmount`) instead of silently taking the dust.\n\nYield lifts every holder's claim because it raises `A` without minting shares. Nobody has to\nclaim anything; withdrawing is the only action.\n\n## 2. `totalAssets()` is accounted, not `balanceOf`\n\nThis is the one design decision worth understanding before touching anything:\n\n```\ntotalAssets() = _storedAssets + (elapsed since last accrual) * _dripRate\npendingYield() = asset.balanceOf(vault) - totalAssets()\n```\n\nTokens sitting in the vault are **not** part of anyone's claim until someone calls `sync()`\n(or the keeper calls `donate()`), and then they are credited **linearly over\n`DRIP_DURATION = 1 days`**, not instantly.\n\nWhy, given the keeper just pushes tokens in:\n\n- **Yield sniping.** With `totalAssets() == balanceOf`, a keeper transfer of yield is a\n  step change in the share price sitting in the public mempool. A bot deposits in front of it,\n  withdraws behind it, and takes a cut of yield it was never exposed to — this is the standard\n  MEV attack on donation-based vaults, and with open withdrawals and no lockup there is nothing\n  else stopping it. Streaming means no lump sum ever lands inside one block, so there is no\n  step to sandwich (`test_YieldSnipingIsUnprofitable`).\n- **Atomic share-price inflation.** A donation made inside a single transaction moves\n  `totalAssets()` by ~0, so the classic first-depositor attack cannot be executed atomically at\n  all. The virtual offset then covers the slow version (`test_InflationAttackDoesNotStealFromVictim`).\n- **Read-only reentrancy.** Because the share price never reads the token balance, an\n  integrator that queries the vault from inside a token-transfer callback still sees a\n  consistent price.\n\nAccepted consequences, in decreasing order of how much they matter:\n\n- Yield that is streaming is shared with anyone who deposits before the stream ends. A large\n  depositor arriving right after a keeper run earns a pro-rata slice of the remaining stream.\n  This is a one-day smear rather than a one-block theft; shortening `DRIP_DURATION` makes\n  sniping easier, lengthening it dilutes short-term depositors more. One day was chosen against\n  a keeper cadence of roughly a day or less.\n- Anyone can call `sync()`, and each call restarts the stream clock for whatever is unvested.\n  Spamming it slightly delays the tail of a stream; it cannot destroy or redirect assets, and it\n  costs the spammer gas. Not worth defending against.\n- If yield is smaller than `DRIP_DURATION` in wei, the per-second rate truncates to 0 and it\n  stays in `pendingYield()` until a later, larger `sync()` sweeps it in. Dust is deferred, never\n  lost (`test_DustBelowOneWeiPerSecondIsNotLost`).\n- If every share is redeemed while a stream is running, the unvested remainder belongs to\n  whoever deposits next.\n\n## 3. Deviations from plain ERC-4626\n\n1. `totalAssets()` is the accounted number above, not the token balance.\n2. `deposit`/`mint` measure the actual balance delta and revert with `AssetTransferShortfall`\n   if less arrived than was priced. So a **fee-on-transfer token's vault simply doesn't accept\n   deposits** — deliberately, because the alternative is minting shares against assets the\n   vault never received, which dilutes everyone already in it (`test_FeeOnTransferDepositReverts`).\n3. Zero-value deposits/redemptions revert rather than no-op.\n\nEverything else — `previewDeposit`, `maxWithdraw`, allowance-based third-party withdrawals,\nthe `Deposit`/`Withdraw` events — is stock OZ behaviour. `nonReentrant` guards every path that\ntouches the asset, on top of checks-effects-interactions ordering (allowance spent and shares\nburned before assets leave).\n\n## 4. Listing a token: what the operator has to get right\n\nThe contracts cannot vet the asset, and the factory deliberately doesn't try. **Being listed is\nnot an endorsement.** The token is arbitrary untrusted code that the vault must hold, so the\nreal safety layer is the frontend allowlist, not the chain. Per token, before it is surfaced\nin any UI:\n\n- **Is the token itself trustworthy?** An upgradeable, mintable, or admin-controlled token can\n  drain, freeze, or inflate its own vault at any time and no vault design can prevent it. This\n  is the single biggest risk in a permissionless listing product. Each vault holds exactly one\n  asset and shares no state with the others, so the blast radius is that token's depositors —\n  keep it that way by never adding cross-vault logic.\n- **Fee-on-transfer?** Deposits revert (§3). Note that a token with a *switchable* fee (USDT\n  has the switch) can turn a working vault into a deposit-blocked one, and existing depositors\n  would then receive slightly less than `withdraw(assets)` asked for. Don't list these.\n- **Rebasing?** Rebase-up is safe (the surplus shows up as `pendingYield` and streams to\n  holders). **Rebase-down is not supported**: the vault's accounted assets would exceed its\n  balance and the last withdrawers would find the vault short. Use the wrapped version\n  (wstETH, not stETH).\n- **Blocklist / pausable?** USDC, USDT and friends can block an address or halt transfers.\n  Deposits and withdrawals then revert until unblocked. Acceptable, but say so in the UI.\n- **Decimals.** Read automatically; over 36 the vault refuses to deploy (`UnsupportedDecimals`).\n  Tokens with no `decimals()` are treated as 18. A token with a bytes32 `symbol()` (MKR) or a\n  missing one gets a `svTOKEN` fallback name — cosmetic only.\n- **Weird ERC-20s to just say no to:** rebasing-down, ERC-777 with hooks (the reentrancy guard\n  makes their vaults DoS-prone rather than exploitable — see `test_ReentrantAssetCannotReenter`),\n  tokens with transfer hooks that can revert selectively, and anything where `balanceOf` is not\n  monotonic under the vault's own actions.\n- **Warn about first-depositor economics** if a vault is empty: the offset makes the inflation\n  attack unprofitable, but a brand-new vault with a dust deposit is still a bad place to be the\n  second depositor at scale. Seeding a small amount at listing is the cheap fix.\n\n## 5. Running the keeper\n\n- **Use `donate(amount)`, not a raw `transfer`.** It pulls the tokens and starts the stream in\n  one transaction, so yield can never sit in the vault uncredited because a second call was\n  dropped. Approve exactly `amount` (or a small multiple of one run's size) — never\n  `type(uint256).max` from a hot keeper key.\n- If yield does arrive by plain transfer, **someone must call `sync()`** or it stays in\n  `pendingYield()` forever, invisible to the share price. `sync()` is permissionless, so\n  anyone (including a depositor) can rescue the situation, but don't rely on that: monitor\n  `pendingYield()` and alert if it is non-zero with no active stream (`dripState()`).\n- **Cadence should be ≥ `DRIP_DURATION` apart, or at least regular.** Syncing more often than\n  the stream length keeps restarting the tail, which slows distribution slightly. Roughly daily\n  runs match the 1-day window.\n- **A donate of 0 reverts**; skip the run instead of sending an empty transaction.\n- Keeper transactions are worth sending through a private mempool (Flashbots Protect). The\n  drip removes the profitable sandwich, but there is no reason to advertise the transfers.\n- The keeper key has **no privileges** — it cannot withdraw, pause, or change anything. A\n  compromised keeper key can donate tokens and nothing else. That is the intended blast radius;\n  don't add an admin function to the vault later without revisiting this.\n- Withdrawals depend only on the vault's own balance, so a keeper that stops running degrades\n  the product to \"0% yield\", never to \"funds stuck\".\n\n## 6. No admin, on purpose\n\nNo owner, no pause, no fee switch, no proxy. On a product whose promise is \"withdraw whenever,\npermissionlessly\", a key that can freeze or upgrade other people's savings is the biggest risk\nin the system, so there isn't one. The cost is real and should be stated plainly:\n\n- Nothing can be paused if a listed token misbehaves. The mitigation is the frontend allowlist\n  and the fact that vaults are isolated.\n- Nothing can be rescued. **Unrelated tokens sent to a vault are stuck forever** (there is no\n  sweep — a sweep would need a privileged destination). Tokens sent to a vault that *are* the\n  vault's asset become yield for its depositors after the next `sync()`.\n- Bugs cannot be fixed in place. A fixed version means a new factory and a migration.\n\nIf a future version needs any of these, it should come with a timelock and a multisig, not an\nEOA — and the tradeoff should be shown to depositors.\n\n## 7. Pre-deploy status\n\nDone here:\n\n- `forge build` clean; `forge test` 20/20 including fuzz runs at 5000 (`--fuzz-runs 5000`).\n- Covered by tests: inflation attack, yield sniping, fee-on-transfer rejection, reentrant\n  asset, zero-value inputs, third-party withdrawal allowance, over-withdrawal, odd metadata,\n  absurd decimals, dust, pro-rata fairness across depositors, non-18-decimal assets (fuzzed\n  over 0–36 decimals).\n\nStill required before mainnet:\n\n- `slither .` (not installed in this environment) and a look at every reentrancy /\n  unchecked-return finding.\n- An external review of the drip accounting, which is the only non-stock math here.\n- `forge verify-contract` for the factory, and verification of the first vault — every later\n  vault has identical bytecode, so explorers will match it automatically. An unverified vault is\n  indistinguishable from a scam to a depositor.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}

Foundry project builds clean, 20/20 tests pass (fuzz at 5000 runs).\n\n**What's there**\n\n- `src/SaveVaultFactory.sol` — permissionless one-vault-per-token registry. `createVault(token)` takes no other parameters on purpose: nothing for a front-runner to set badly, and listing grants no privilege over the token. Safe untrusted-token metadata reads (missing/reverting/bytes32 `symbol()`, oversized-string grief).\n- `src/SaveVault.sol` — OZ v5 ERC-4626, shares *are* the transferable receipt. No owner, no fees, no pause, no proxy.\n- `test/SaveVault.t.sol` + mocks, `script/Deploy.s.sol`, `NOTES.md`.\n\n**Three decisions that drove the code**\n\n1. **`totalAssets()` is accounted, not `balanceOf`.** Incoming tokens are credited via `sync()`/`donate()` and stream in linearly over 1 day. With balance-based accounting, the keeper's yield transfer is a share-price step change sitting in the public mempool — a bot deposits in front, withdraws behind, and takes yield it was never exposed to. Open withdrawals with no lockup means nothing else stops that. The stream also makes atomic share-price inflation impossible and keeps the price immune to read-only reentrancy.\n2. **Virtual-share offset (`_decimalsOffset() == 3`)** for the non-atomic inflation attack. Receipt decimals = asset decimals + 3, so a USDC vault's receipt is 9 decimals — no hardcoded `1e18` anywhere; assets over 36 decimals refuse to deploy.\n3. **Deposits must deliver what they were priced on.** `_deposit` checks the balance delta and reverts (`AssetTransferShortfall`), so a fee-on-transfer vault takes no deposits rather than minting shares against assets that never arrived. `nonReentrant` on every asset-touching path, on top of CEI.\n\n**Worth flagging:** since listing is permissionless, the token is untrusted code the vault must hold — a malicious or upgradeable asset can drain its own vault and no vault design prevents that. Vaults are isolated so the blast radius is that token's depositors; the real safety layer is the frontend allowlist. Relatedly, \"no admin\" means nothing can be paused or rescued, and unrelated tokens sent to a vault are stuck forever. Both tradeoffs are written up in NOTES.md §4/§6 rather than silently taken.\n\nTwo gaps I couldn't close here: `slither` isn't installed in this environment, and the drip accounting is the only non-stock math in the system, so it should get external review before mainnet. Both are listed in NOTES.md §7 alongside source verification."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":317,"cache_read_input_tokens":103703,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":317},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"1a0747da-09d0-40ee-9231-f80412a577ad","uuid":"d8c332d6-2d0a-4f22-a3a4-d8942697d38e","timestamp":"2026-07-28T12:38:07.429Z","request_id":"req_011CdUU6ZhL1SSBCapvbgdt9"}
